programs.name: Disabled Veterans' Property Tax Exemption
programs.agency: California State Board of Equalization (BOE) — filed with your county assessor
programs.eligibility: Veteran rated 100% service-connected disabled by the USDVA (or compensated at the 100% rate due to individual unemployability), who served during a qualifying wartime/eligibility period and was discharged under other-than-dishonorable conditions. Also available to an unmarried surviving spouse of such a veteran or of one who died from a service-connected cause. Applies to the claimant's principal place of residence.
programs.coverage: For the 2026 lien year, the exemption reduces assessed value by $180,671 (Basic, no income limit) or $271,009 (Low-Income). The Low-Income tier requires household income at or below $81,131 (2026) and annual recertification. Amounts adjust each year by the California CPI. File BOE-261-G with the county assessor.
programs.notes: The Basic exemption has no income limit and no annual recertification; only claim the Low-Income tier if your household income is under the limit, since it must be re-filed yearly.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran (DV) License Plates with Registration Fee Exemption
programs.agency: California Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV)
programs.eligibility: Veteran permanently disabled from a service-connected injury or disease who meets any of: rated 100% disabled by the USDVA for a condition that substantially impairs mobility; cannot move without an assistive device; lost the use of one or more limbs; or is permanently blind. Requires DMV form REG 256V with medical certification (or certification from a County Veterans Service Officer / CalVet / USDVA representative).
programs.coverage: DV License Plates exempt the qualifying veteran from vehicle registration and license fees. The exemption applies to one vehicle owned by the disabled veteran and displaying the DV plates.
programs.notes: The fee exemption covers only one vehicle; the vehicle must be owned by the veteran and bear the DV plates.

programs.name: Reduced-Fee Disabled Veteran Hunting and Sport Fishing Licenses
programs.agency: California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW)
programs.eligibility: Honorably discharged veterans with a VA service-connected disability rating of 50% or greater. Must prequalify by submitting a VA Benefit Summary Letter certifying honorable discharge and the 50%+ rating.
programs.coverage: Reduced-fee annual licenses (Disabled Veteran Sport Fishing and Disabled Veteran Hunting) at a small fraction of the standard resident fee. Purchase online, at a CDFW License Sales Office, or at a license agent after prequalifying.
programs.notes: This is a reduced fee, not free. California's separate FREE recreational license program for the visually/mobility/developmentally disabled is distinct from this veteran reduced-fee license.

programs.name: Veterans Homes of California (Long-Term Care)
programs.agency: California Department of Veterans Affairs (CalVet)
programs.eligibility: California-resident veterans discharged under honorable conditions, generally age 55+ (age waived for disabled or homeless veterans needing long-term care); eligible spouses/domestic partners may also be admitted. Priority for Medal of Honor recipients, former POWs, wartime veterans, homeless veterans, and those rated 70%+ service-connected disabled.
programs.coverage: Eight homes statewide — Yountville, Barstow, Chula Vista, West Los Angeles, Fresno, Lancaster, Ventura, and Redding — offering a continuum from independent/domiciliary living and residential care through intermediate care and 24/7 skilled nursing (memory care at some sites).
programs.notes: Levels of care and bed availability vary by home; apply online via CalVet or by paper application. Confirm a specific home's current address/availability on the CalVet Veterans Home Directory.

programs.name: State Income Tax on Military Retired Pay (Partial Exclusion)
programs.agency: California Franchise Tax Board (FTB)
programs.eligibility: California residents receiving federal uniformed-services retirement pay or a DoD Survivor Benefit Plan annuity. Income limits: federal AGI up to $125,000 (single/HoH) or up to $250,000 (married filing jointly/surviving spouse).
programs.coverage: Military retired pay IS taxable in California, but for tax years 2025–2029 qualified taxpayers may exclude up to $20,000 of military retirement pay (or SBP annuity) from state taxable income. This is California's first such exemption; before 2025 military retired pay was fully taxed. The exclusion is scheduled to sunset after the 2029 tax year unless extended.
programs.notes: Claim the exclusion on Schedule CA (540/540NR). Above the AGI thresholds there is no exclusion and the full retired pay is taxed at California's ordinary income rates.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran Residence Homestead Property Tax Exemption
programs.agency: Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts (administered by county appraisal districts)
programs.eligibility: Texas resident veterans with a VA service-connected disability rating, applied via Form 50-135 to the local appraisal district. Veterans rated 100% disabled (or with individual unemployability) qualify for the full exemption under a separate provision. Unmarried surviving spouses may qualify if the property remains their homestead.
programs.coverage: Partial exemption of assessed value by disability tier: 10–29% = $5,000; 30–49% = $7,500; 50–69% = $10,000; 70–100% = $12,000. Additional $12,000 if age 65+ with a 10%+ rating, totally blind in one or both eyes, or loss of use of one or more limbs. Separately, a 100% disabled (or individual-unemployability) veteran receives an exemption of the TOTAL appraised value of the homestead (full exemption).
programs.notes: The 100% full exemption is detailed at comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/property-tax/exemptions/disabledvet-100-faq.php. A surviving spouse of a service member killed in the line of duty may receive a full homestead exemption if unmarried. (Tex. Tax Code Sec. 11.22.)

programs.name: Disabled Veteran (DV) License Plates & Registration Fee Exemption
programs.agency: Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV)
programs.eligibility: Veteran with a service-connected disability of at least 50%, OR at least 40% due to amputation of a lower extremity, receiving VA compensation for that disability. Apply with Form VTR-615 through the county tax assessor-collector.
programs.coverage: First set of DV plates: $3 annual fee, with most other registration fees waived on that one vehicle. Additional sets have no plate fee, but the registration-fee exemption applies to only one vehicle. DV plates also exempt the vehicle from state/local parking-meter fees when transporting the veteran.
programs.notes: Surviving spouses of qualifying disabled veterans also pay $3 for the first set, additional sets free. Confirmed via the TxDMV 'For Our Troops' page and the official VTR-428 DV Plate Brochure.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran 'Super Combo' Hunting & All-Water Fishing Package (Free)
programs.agency: Texas Parks & Wildlife Department (TPWD)
programs.eligibility: Resident OR non-resident qualifying as a disabled veteran per the VA: loss of use of a foot or leg, OR a disability rating of 50% or more, AND receiving compensation from the U.S. for the disability. Proof of disability (VA-issued, dated within the last 12 months) or a Texas Driver License with 'Disabled Veteran' designation must be shown each year.
programs.coverage: FREE Super Combo package, which includes five state endorsements (all except the Reptile and Amphibian endorsement). Available in person only at a license retailer.
programs.notes: The federal Duck Stamp is NOT included and is still required for waterfowl hunting. Confirmed directly from the TPWD package page.

programs.name: Texas State Veterans Homes (Long-Term Nursing Care)
programs.agency: Texas Veterans Land Board (VLB) / Texas General Land Office, with Texas HHSC and the USDVA
programs.eligibility: Recognized as an 'eligible veteran' by the USDVA, no dishonorable discharge, requiring physician-determined long-term nursing care (USDVA-concurred), at least 18, and a bona fide Texas resident at application, at entry into military service, or resident in Texas for at least one continuous year before applying. Spouses/unmarried surviving spouses and Gold Star parents may also qualify under the residency rule.
programs.coverage: Ten state veterans homes statewide (including Amarillo, Big Spring, Bonham, El Paso, McAllen, and Fort Worth). Affordable long-term skilled nursing care plus physical/occupational/speech and other therapies; care funded in part through VA per-diem benefits. Veterans with a 70%+ service-connected disability can generally live in the homes for free.
programs.notes: Operated by the VLB/General Land Office, NOT the Texas Veterans Commission (TVC handles claims, 800-252-VETS). Full home roster at glo.texas.gov/veterans/veterans-homes/locations.

programs.name: State Income Tax on Military Retired Pay (None)
programs.agency: State of Texas (Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts)
programs.eligibility: All Texas residents, including military retirees.
programs.coverage: No state tax on military retired pay. Texas has NO personal/individual state income tax, so military retirement pay and VA disability compensation are fully untaxed at the state level (federal income tax may still apply to retired pay).
programs.notes: Texas is one of the states with no individual income tax; there is no exemption statute because no income tax exists.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran $5,000 Property Tax Exemption (10%+ disability)
programs.agency: Florida Department of Revenue / County Property Appraiser
programs.eligibility: Honorably discharged ex-servicemember, Florida resident, with a service-connected disability of 10% or more (or disabled by misfortune while serving during wartime). Surviving spouse may carry over under certain circumstances.
programs.coverage: $5,000 reduction in the property's assessed value. Not limited to homestead property.
programs.notes: Authorized under s. 196.24, F.S. Apply via Form DR-501 with the county property appraiser.

programs.name: Total Property Tax Exemption for Service-Connected Total & Permanent Disability
programs.agency: Florida Department of Revenue / County Property Appraiser
programs.eligibility: Florida-resident veteran, honorably discharged, with a service-connected total and permanent disability. A similar full exemption is available to disabled veterans confined to wheelchairs. Surviving spouse may carry over under certain circumstances.
programs.coverage: 100% (total) exemption from ad valorem taxes on property owned and used as a homestead.
programs.notes: Authorized under ss. 196.081 and 196.091, F.S. Apply via Form DR-501 with the county property appraiser.

programs.name: Property Tax Discount for Combat-Related Disabled Veterans 65 or Older
programs.agency: Florida Department of Revenue / County Property Appraiser
programs.eligibility: Veteran age 65 or older who is partially or totally permanently disabled (combat-related, service-connected), who owns and uses the property as a homestead and meets statutory requirements. Discount carries over to a surviving spouse who holds title, permanently resides there, and has not remarried.
programs.coverage: Discount on assessed value equal to the percentage of the veteran's permanent service-connected disability as determined by the USDVA (e.g., a 50% rating = 50% discount).
programs.notes: Authorized under s. 196.082, F.S. Apply via Form DR-501. A separate deployed-servicemember exemption (s. 196.173, F.S., Form DR-501M) prorates exemption by days deployed on a designated operation.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran 'DV' License Plate & Free Vehicle Registration
programs.agency: Florida Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles (FLHSMV)
programs.eligibility: 100% disabled veterans. Issued at a county tax collector office or license plate agency.
programs.coverage: 'DV' license plate issued at no charge on all motor vehicles except mobile homes, commercial vehicles, and trucks over 26,000 lbs GVW.
programs.notes: Authorized under s. 320.084, F.S. Per SB 736 (2024), a DV-eligible veteran may instead elect a military or specialty plate but must pay applicable fees beyond those otherwise waived; only one free plate.

programs.name: Resident Persons with Disabilities Hunting & Fishing License (Disabled Veterans)
programs.agency: Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission (FWC)
programs.eligibility: Florida resident, honorably discharged, certified by the USDVA (or a branch of the U.S. Armed Forces) as having a service-connected disability of 50% or greater.
programs.coverage: No-cost (free) combined license, 5-year term. Includes saltwater fishing, freshwater fishing, and hunting, plus Deer, Wildlife Management Area, Archery, Muzzleloading Gun, Crossbow, Turkey, Florida Waterfowl, Snook, and Lobster permits.
programs.notes: Apply at GoOutdoorsFlorida.com or a county tax collector's office with proof of residency and disability. Federal Duck Stamp still required for waterfowl. Active-duty/retired residents may alternatively qualify for the Military Gold Sportsman's License.

programs.name: State Veterans' Nursing Homes & Assisted Living Facility
programs.agency: Florida Department of Veterans' Affairs (FDVA)
programs.eligibility: Honorable discharge, Florida residency prior to admission, and certification of need for skilled nursing or assisted living care by a VA physician. Eligible spouses may also be admitted.
programs.coverage: Six state veterans' skilled-nursing homes (Daytona Beach, Land O' Lakes, Pembroke Pines, Panama City, Port Charlotte, St. Augustine) plus one assisted living facility (Lake City). Several offer dedicated memory care beds.
programs.notes: Operated by FDVA in partnership with the USDVA. Apply via the FDVA application packet.

programs.name: State Income Tax on Military Retired Pay (None)
programs.agency: State of Florida (Florida Department of Revenue)
programs.eligibility: All Florida residents, including military retirees.
programs.coverage: Florida levies NO state personal income tax of any kind. Military retired pay, active-duty pay, VA disability compensation, and Survivor Benefit Plan payments are entirely exempt from state income tax.
programs.notes: A state income tax is prohibited by the Florida Constitution (Article VII, Section 5).

programs.name: Real Property Tax Exemption for 100% Service-Connected Disabled Veterans
programs.agency: Local Commissioner of the Revenue (authorized by Code of Virginia § 58.1-3219.5)
programs.eligibility: Veteran with a 100% service-connected, permanent and total disability rating from the USDVA, OR a VA rating of individual unemployability. Unremarried surviving spouse of a qualifying veteran, or of a service member killed in the line of duty, also qualifies.
programs.coverage: 100% exemption of real estate tax on the principal residence plus up to one acre of land. No income limit and no home-value cap.
programs.notes: Statewide mandatory exemption. File VA certification with the local Commissioner of the Revenue; once granted it continues automatically though the locality may periodically reverify. Applies only to the principal residence.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran (DV) License Plates & Registration Fee Waiver
programs.agency: Virginia Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV)
programs.eligibility: Free DV plates and fee waiver: veteran who has lost (or lost the use of) an arm, hand, or leg, is blind, or is rated permanently and totally disabled by the VA. Any veteran with a VA-certified service-connected disability may obtain DV plates by paying the standard fees.
programs.coverage: One set of DV plates free for qualifying (lost-limb/blind/P&T) veterans; no annual registration fee on one personally owned vehicle for that veteran or unremarried surviving spouse. Other service-connected disabled veterans pay normal registration plus a $10 special-plate fee. (Code of Virginia § 46.2-739.)
programs.notes: Virginia also offers a one-time motor-vehicle Sales and Use Tax exemption for veterans rated 100% service-connected permanent and total.

programs.name: Lifetime Hunting & Fishing Licenses for Resident Disabled Veterans
programs.agency: Virginia Department of Wildlife Resources (DWR)
programs.eligibility: Virginia residents with a VA service-connected disability rating. A rating of at least 30% qualifies for a reduced/discounted lifetime license; veterans rated totally and permanently (100%) service-connected disabled qualify for a FREE lifetime license. Requires a VA Benefit Summary Letter or Certificate of Disability.
programs.coverage: Free lifetime hunting, freshwater fishing, and trapping licenses for totally-and-permanently service-connected disabled residents; reduced-fee lifetime licenses for other qualifying ratings (fee scaled by rating).
programs.notes: The free 100%-P&T tier and the 30%+ eligibility floor are confirmed; the exact reduced-fee dollar amounts by rating tier vary — confirm the current fee on the DWR site before relying on a specific number.

programs.name: Virginia Veterans Care Centers (State Veterans Homes)
programs.agency: Virginia Department of Veterans Services (DVS)
programs.eligibility: Honorably discharged veteran who is a Virginia resident at admission (or who entered active duty from Virginia). Post-1980/1981 enlistees must meet the minimum-active-duty requirement; Reserve/Guard must have served the full period of a federal active-duty order.
programs.coverage: State-operated skilled-nursing/long-term care (some also offer memory care and short-term rehab). Cost is based on VA per-diem, the veteran's VA disability status, and ability to pay; it is not categorically free.
programs.notes: Facilities: Sitter & Barfoot (Richmond), Jones & Cabacoy (Virginia Beach), Puller (Fauquier County), and Davis & McDaniel (Roanoke). Admission is application/availability-based.

programs.name: Military Benefits Income Tax Subtraction (Retired Pay)
programs.agency: Virginia Department of Taxation
programs.eligibility: Recipients of eligible military benefits — military retirement income, qualified military benefits, and Survivor Benefit Plan payments to a surviving spouse. No age requirement (the former age-55 minimum was eliminated effective tax year 2024).
programs.coverage: Per current Virginia Tax guidance, the subtraction is capped at $40,000 of eligible military benefits for tax year 2025 and later (phase-in was $10,000 TY2022, $20,000 TY2023, $30,000 TY2024, $40,000 TY2025+).
programs.notes: Verify the current cap on tax.virginia.gov before relying on it: 2025/2026 General Assembly bills proposed removing the cap entirely (CPI-adjusted) effective TY2026, but as of this writing that change is not reflected in official Tax Department guidance.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran Property Tax Homestead Exclusion
programs.agency: NC Department of Revenue / county tax offices (certified via NC Division of Veterans Affairs)
programs.eligibility: Honorably (or under honorable conditions) discharged veteran with a permanent and total 100% service-connected disability, OR who receives VA benefits for specially adapted housing under 38 U.S.C. 2101. Also available to the unremarried surviving spouse. Must own and occupy the home as of January 1. No income limit. Certify with Form NCDVA-9 plus Form AV-9 (deadline June 1).
programs.coverage: Excludes the first $45,000 of the appraised/assessed value of the permanent residence from property tax (G.S. 105-277.1C).
programs.notes: Statutory amount fixed at $45,000. Distinct from NC's separate elderly/disabled low-income homestead programs.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran (DV) License Plate
programs.agency: NC Division of Motor Vehicles (NCDMV) with NC Division of Veterans Affairs certification
programs.eligibility: Veteran with a VA combined disability rating of 100%, OR rated Individual Unemployability and paid at the 100% rate. Lower ratings receive a Partially Disabled Veteran plate (not free). Apply on Form MVR-33A with DD-214 and a current VA rating letter, certified by a DMVA Accredited Veterans Service Officer.
programs.coverage: One Disabled Veteran plate issued free of the license plate fee. Several other special plates (Medal of Honor, Ex-POW, Silver Star, etc.) are also free.
programs.notes: The 'free' applies to the special-plate fee; standard registration and personalization fees may still apply per DMV.

programs.name: Lifetime Hunting & Fishing License for Resident Disabled Veterans
programs.agency: NC Wildlife Resources Commission (NCWRC)
programs.eligibility: NC resident who is a 50%-or-more disabled veteran as determined by the USDVA; valid for life so long as the veteran remains 50%+ disabled; VA certification required. (A separate Totally Disabled Resident lifetime license exists for residents certified totally disabled by SSA, CSRS, RRB, or the NC State Retirement System.)
programs.coverage: Reduced/discounted lifetime license combining hunting and inland fishing privileges (one-time fee, far below standard lifetime sportsman pricing).
programs.notes: Lifetime — remains usable even if the holder later moves out of state. Confirm the current exact fee on the NCWRC fee schedule before relying on a specific number.

programs.name: North Carolina State Veterans Homes (Skilled Nursing Care)
programs.agency: NC Department of Military and Veterans Affairs (DMVA)
programs.eligibility: Veteran who served on active duty for other than training with an honorable (or under honorable conditions) discharge; NC resident for at least the 24 months immediately preceding application; disabled by age, disease, or other cause; referred by a licensed physician (FL-2 form signed within 30 days) as needing skilled nursing care.
programs.coverage: 24-hour skilled nursing and rehabilitative care. Accepts Medicare, Medicaid, private pay, and commercial insurance.
programs.notes: Operating facilities: Salisbury, Black Mountain, Kinston, and Kernersville. The Fayetteville home is closed for replacement. Admissions: DMVA (919) 807-4263.

programs.name: State Income-Tax Exemption (Deduction) for Military Retired Pay
programs.agency: NC Department of Revenue (NCDOR)
programs.eligibility: Retired member of the uniformed services who either (1) served at least 20 years, OR (2) was medically retired under 10 U.S.C. Chapter 61. Survivor Benefit Plan beneficiaries may deduct payments from a plan defined in 10 U.S.C. § 1447. Allowed only to the extent the pay is included in federal AGI.
programs.coverage: 100% deduction (full exemption) of qualifying military retired pay and qualifying SBP survivor payments from NC taxable income.
programs.notes: Enacted by 2021 budget law, effective for tax years beginning on or after Jan 1, 2022; confirmed active for 2026. Separate from the older Bailey v. State exemption (for members vested as of Aug 12, 1989).

programs.name: Disabled Veteran Homestead Tax Exemption
programs.agency: Georgia Department of Veterans Service (administered by county tax commissioners) / Georgia Department of Revenue
programs.eligibility: Georgia resident veteran, honorably discharged, who is VA-rated 100% totally disabled; OR rated less than 100% but paid at the 100% rate due to individual unemployability; OR entitled to VA statutory awards for loss/loss of use of hands, feet, or sight. Extends to the unremarried surviving spouse and surviving minor children while they occupy the home.
programs.coverage: $121,812 deducted from the 40% assessed value of the homestead (2025 figure currently in effect); the amount is indexed annually to the federal figure under 38 U.S.C. 2102. Property value above the exemption remains taxable. Applies across state, county, municipal, and school ad valorem taxes.
programs.notes: Apply through your county tax commissioner. The exemption amount rises most years with federal indexing — confirm the current year's figure with your county before relying on it.

programs.name: Free Disabled Veteran (DV) License Plate
programs.agency: Georgia Department of Veterans Service / Georgia Department of Revenue, Motor Vehicle Division
programs.eligibility: Honorably discharged Georgia-resident veteran who is VA-rated 100% totally disabled, or who has a VA statutory award for loss/loss of use of feet, hands, or sight. Also available to unremarried surviving spouses (and minor children) of qualified deceased veterans.
programs.coverage: No registration fee, manufacturing fee, or annual fee. Allowed on up to 2 motorcycles or passenger vehicles for personal use. Veterans with a 100% service-connected rating are also exempt from ad valorem (title) tax on one vehicle.
programs.notes: Statutory basis O.C.G.A. 40-2-69. Motor homes excluded. Apply via local county tag office (with VA letter) or a GDVS Veterans Field Service Office.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran / Veterans Hunting & Fishing Licenses
programs.agency: Georgia Department of Natural Resources, Wildlife Resources Division (with GDVS)
programs.eligibility: Disability Sportsman's License: Georgia resident with a permanent and total VA disability rating (provide VA Benefit Summary letter, residency proof, and the WRD Certification of Disability application; not available online). One-Time Veterans License (separate): Georgia resident who served 90+ days active federal duty and was honorably discharged on/after July 1, 2005.
programs.coverage: Disability Sportsman's License (full hunting + big game + migratory bird + salt/freshwater fishing + trout): $18.00 for 3 years or $8.00 annual. Hunting-only or fishing-only: $12.00/3 years or $6.00 annual. One-Time Veterans License: FREE, full sportsman privileges, valid 1 year, issued once. Totally blind residents qualify for a free lifetime honorary fishing license.
programs.notes: The disability license is steeply discounted (not free) for disabled vets; the only free veteran license is the one-time post-9/11-era license. Both administered jointly by GDVS and DNR (800-366-2661).

programs.name: Georgia War Veterans Homes (Milledgeville & Augusta)
programs.agency: Georgia Department of Veterans Service
programs.eligibility: Skilled nursing care for war veterans who are domiciled in Georgia (resided 2 years immediately preceding application OR 5 of the last 15 years); served on active duty during a recognized wartime period; were discharged under other than dishonorable conditions; are VA-approved as eligible for skilled nursing care; and are free of contagious disease and serious behavioral/psychiatric problems.
programs.coverage: A nominal daily fee applies. For veterans with a service-connected disability rating of 70% or higher, or whose admission is for a service-connected condition, the VA pays the daily fee in full ($0 to the veteran). Others may apply for VA Aid & Attendance to offset the fee.
programs.notes: Two locations: Milledgeville (478-445-4295) and Augusta. Both are state-owned skilled nursing facilities for eligible wartime veterans.

programs.name: State Income-Tax Exclusion of Military Retirement Pay
programs.agency: Georgia Department of Revenue
programs.eligibility: Individuals receiving military retirement benefits. Stacks with Georgia's general retirement income exclusion for those age 62+ or permanently and totally disabled (but the same income cannot use both the military exclusion and the general exclusion).
programs.coverage: For tax year 2026: military exclusion up to $17,500 for taxpayers under 62, plus an additional $17,500 if the taxpayer has more than $17,500 of Georgia earned income; veterans 62–64 may instead use the general retirement exclusion (up to $35,000) and 65+ (up to $65,000). Beginning tax year 2027 (HB 266, signed May 13, 2025), the military exclusion rises to up to $65,000 for individuals under age 65.
programs.notes: Verified against the enrolled HB 266 (O.C.G.A. 48-7-27). The $65,000/under-65 expansion takes effect tax year 2027 (NOT 2026) and is age-capped at under 65, despite some secondary sources stating otherwise.

programs.name: Disabled Veterans' Real Estate Tax Exemption
programs.agency: PA Department of Military and Veterans Affairs (DMVA) / State Veterans' Commission; administered through County Veterans Affairs Directors
programs.eligibility: Honorably discharged PA-resident wartime veteran with a 100% permanent total service-connected disability rating (or, from military service, blind, paraplegic, or loss of two or more limbs), who has a financial need. Annual income of $114,637 or less (effective Jan 1, 2025) is presumed to meet the need test; above that, income vs. expenses are compared. Veterans benefits are now excluded from the income assessment. Unremarried surviving spouses may continue the exemption.
programs.coverage: 100% exemption from real estate (property) tax on the veteran's principal residence (dwelling and the land it sits on). Recertification typically every 5 years.
programs.notes: Apply through your County Veterans Affairs Director. The income threshold is indexed and rises over time; veterans previously denied for financial need are encouraged to reapply due to the new benefits-exclusion law.

programs.name: Free Vehicle Registration for Eligible Veterans & Disabled Veteran Plate
programs.agency: PennDOT — Driver and Vehicle Services
programs.eligibility: One passenger vehicle or truck of 9,000 lbs or less owned by a veteran who, from military service: lost a limb or an eye or became permanently paralyzed; OR was a prisoner of war; OR was awarded the Medal of Honor; OR was awarded the Purple Heart.
programs.coverage: Registration fee and title fee waived ($0). The license PLATE fee is charged separately (e.g., the Severely Disabled Veteran plate carries an $11 fee). Separate 'Disabled Veteran' / 'Severely Disabled Veteran' special plates available via form MV-145V / MV-371DV.
programs.notes: Eligibility on the official free-registration page is condition-based (limb/eye loss, paralysis, POW, MOH, Purple Heart) — not a blanket 'any 100% disabled' rule.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran Hunting & Fishing Licenses
programs.agency: PA Game Commission (hunting) / PA Fish and Boat Commission (fishing)
programs.eligibility: Pennsylvania resident with a VA-certified service-connected disability. Free license for those who are blind or certified 100% disabled; reduced-fee license for those rated 60–99% (service-connected, injuries received in time of war or armed conflict). VA documentation required.
programs.coverage: Free hunting/furtaker license and free fishing license (with a free Combination Trout/Lake Erie Permit) for 100%/blind veterans. Disabled-veteran antlerless deer licenses at the resident fee ($6.97) and guaranteed in the WMU of choice. Reduced-fee licenses for 60–99% disabled.
programs.notes: Initial/free applications processed at county treasurers, the commission offices, or regional offices; renewals at any issuing agent or online.

programs.name: Pennsylvania State Veterans' Homes (Six Locations)
programs.agency: PA Department of Military and Veterans Affairs (DMVA)
programs.eligibility: Veteran who served in the U.S. Armed Forces or PA Military Forces and was discharged under honorable conditions; must be a bona fide PA resident or have had PA as home of record upon entry into service. Spouses and surviving spouses may also be admitted. Levels of care vary (skilled nursing, personal care, domiciliary).
programs.coverage: Residents make monthly payments against a maintenance-fee liability based on ability to pay (income/assets); VA per-diem payments offset cost for eligible veterans.
programs.notes: Six homes: Delaware Valley (NE Philadelphia), Gino J. Merli (Scranton), Hollidaysburg, PA Soldiers' & Sailors' Home (Erie), Southeastern (Spring City), and Southwestern (near Pittsburgh).

programs.name: State Income Tax on Military Retired Pay (Exempt)
programs.agency: PA Department of Revenue
programs.eligibility: All PA residents receiving qualifying military retired/retainer pay calculated under Chapter 71 of Title 10, U.S. Code.
programs.coverage: 100% exempt from Pennsylvania personal income tax (flat 3.07% rate). No age or income limit. Local Earned Income Tax also does not reach retirement/pension income.
programs.notes: Confirmed via the official PA Personal Income Tax Guide. Active-duty pay rules differ (active duty inside PA by a PA resident is generally taxable) — separate from the retired-pay exemption.

programs.name: Enhanced Homestead Exemption for Disabled Veterans
programs.agency: Ohio Department of Taxation (administered by county auditors)
programs.eligibility: Honorably discharged veteran with a 100% service-connected disability rating, OR rated/compensated at the 100% level due to individual unemployability (TDIU). No age or income limit. Surviving spouses of qualifying veterans may also qualify. Apply via form DTE 105I.
programs.coverage: Exempts up to $58,000 of the home's true (market) value from property taxation (tax year 2025; statutory base of $50,000 indexed annually by the GDP deflator per ORC 323.152). Actual dollar savings depend on the local tax rate.
programs.notes: This 'enhanced' exemption is roughly double the standard senior/disabled exemption. Confirm the current tax-year indexed figure with your county auditor, as it adjusts annually.

programs.name: Veterans with Disabilities License Plate (Free Registration)
programs.agency: Ohio Bureau of Motor Vehicles (BMV)
programs.eligibility: Veteran with a service-connected disability rated or compensated at 100% by the VA, OR who received a VA monetary allowance toward the purchase of a motor vehicle due to service-connected disabilities. Requires a VA award letter (dated within the past year).
programs.coverage: No registration fee, service fee, local motor vehicle (permissive) tax, or registration-transfer fee. One plate issued at no charge; eligible veterans may instead obtain up to two free military plates they qualify for.
programs.notes: Statutory basis ORC 4503.41. Contact BMV Registration Support Services (614) 752-7518.

programs.name: Free Hunting & Fishing Licenses for Disabled Veterans and Former POWs
programs.agency: Ohio Department of Natural Resources, Division of Wildlife (certified by Ohio Dept. of Veterans Services)
programs.eligibility: Ohio resident (resided in Ohio the last 6 consecutive months) who is either a former prisoner of war, OR a veteran with a 100% service-connected (permanent and total) disability who receives VA pension or compensation. Application certified by the Ohio Dept. of Veterans Services using form DNR 9032-B.
programs.coverage: Free: fishing license, hunting license, fur taker permit, deer permit, wild turkey permit, and/or wetlands habitat stamp (any combination). Issued for a 5-year period.
programs.notes: Statutory basis ORC 1533.12. Status updates via 1-800-WILDLIFE.

programs.name: Ohio Veterans Homes (Sandusky & Georgetown)
programs.agency: Ohio Department of Veterans Services (DVS)
programs.eligibility: Ohio citizen for at least one year; most recent discharge honorable or under honorable conditions; served on active duty (other than for training) during a period of war or declared armed conflict OR received the Armed Forces Expeditionary Medal or Vietnam Service Medal; and determined by medical authority to be disabled and incapable of earning a living by reason of that disability.
programs.coverage: Long-term care at two campuses. Both Sandusky and Georgetown provide licensed nursing-home care (Standard, Memory/Dementia, and Skilled Care). Sandusky also offers an independent/limited-supervised-living Domiciliary. Costs are based on care level and resident income.
programs.notes: Apply directly to Sandusky or Georgetown (OVH Admission Application); may apply for the first available bed at either home.

programs.name: State Income Tax on Military Retired Pay (Exempt)
programs.agency: Ohio Department of Taxation
programs.eligibility: Recipients of retired/retainer pay from the uniformed services, including Survivor Benefit Plan (SBP) and RCSBP annuity recipients. No age or income limit.
programs.coverage: 100% of military retirement pay is deductible from Ohio adjusted gross income (fully exempt), claimed as a 'uniformed services retirement income' deduction on the Ohio Schedule of Adjustments.
programs.notes: Long-standing full exemption, distinct from the separately treated active-duty/National Guard pay. Ordinary federal civil-service/non-military pensions are NOT covered.

programs.name: Alternative Veterans' Exemption (Real Property Tax)
programs.agency: NYS Department of Taxation and Finance (administered by local assessors)
programs.eligibility: Veteran who served during a defined period of war (or qualifying spouse/widow(er)); property must be the veteran's primary residence. File Form RP-458-a with the municipal assessor (deadline typically March 1; verify locally). Proof of honorable discharge or a Restoration of Honor Act letter required.
programs.coverage: 15% reduction in assessed value for wartime service; additional 10% for combat-zone service; additional reduction equal to one-half of the service-connected disability rating. Percentages are subject to maximum dollar caps set by each taxing jurisdiction. Maximum combined exemption is 75% of assessed value.
programs.notes: The most commonly used of NY's three veteran property-tax exemptions (also the older Eligible Funds and Cold War Veterans' exemptions). Dollar caps and which exemption is offered vary by municipality, county, and school district.

programs.name: Motor Vehicle Registration Fee Exemption & Veteran License Plates
programs.agency: NYS Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) / NYS Dept. of Veterans' Services
programs.eligibility: Registration-fee and plate-fee exemption applies to veterans who received federal funds for a specially adapted vehicle for a service-connected disability (38 U.S.C. Ch. 39), or who qualify for Medal of Honor or Prisoner of War custom plates. Separate Disabled Veteran and veteran custom plates are available more broadly.
programs.coverage: $0 registration fee and $0 plate fee for those meeting the adapted-vehicle / MOH / POW criteria. Fee-exempt registrants may also enroll in the NYS Thruway Disabled Veteran Non-Revenue E-ZPass for free Thruway travel. Standard 'Disabled American Veteran' custom plates otherwise carry an annual custom-plate fee.
programs.notes: The fee exemption is narrower than 'any disabled veteran' — it is tied to the adapted-vehicle federal grant or MOH/POW status. Apply at any NYS DMV office.

programs.name: Reduced-Fee Hunting, Fishing & Trapping Licenses for Disabled Veterans
programs.agency: NYS Department of Environmental Conservation (DEC)
programs.eligibility: New York State residents with a 40% or greater service-related disability, verified by a VA letter stating the case number and a service-connected disability of 40%+. Proof submitted once is retained on file.
programs.coverage: $5 for the first fishing, hunting, or trapping license purchased within a calendar year; additional purchases of those license types are free through Dec 31 of that year. Bowhunting and muzzleloading privileges are free (with a base hunting license). Also receive preference on Deer Management Permit selection.
programs.notes: A reduced/low-fee program, not a free lifetime license.

programs.name: New York State Veterans Homes (Skilled Nursing)
programs.agency: NYS Department of Health and State University of New York (SUNY)
programs.eligibility: Honorably discharged U.S. Armed Forces veteran with a minimum of 30 days active service who requires skilled nursing care, and who either entered active duty from New York or has been a NY resident for one year prior to application. Qualified spouses and Gold Star parents may also be admitted, subject to bed availability.
programs.coverage: Five state-operated facilities: St. Albans (Jamaica), Batavia, Oxford, Montrose, and Long Island (Stony Brook). Care is provided with no means test; eligible veterans generally have no out-of-pocket cost (offset by VA per-diem, Medicare/Medicaid). Veterans rated 70%+ service-connected receive full VA coverage.
programs.notes: Owned/operated by NYS DOH and SUNY (not the federal VA). Admission via apps.health.ny.gov/nysvets or facility admissions offices.

programs.name: State Income Tax on Military Retired Pay (Exempt)
programs.agency: NYS Department of Taxation and Finance
programs.eligibility: Retired U.S. military personnel and their beneficiaries receiving military pension payments.
programs.coverage: 100% exempt. Military pension payments are totally exempt from New York State, New York City, and Yonkers income taxes. Reported as a NY subtraction modification on Form IT-225.
programs.notes: Confirmed directly from tax.ny.gov. Distinct from active-duty pay rules, which depend on residency/combat-zone status.

programs.name: Property Tax Exemption for Veterans with Disabilities
programs.agency: Washington State Department of Revenue (DOR) / county assessors; info via WA Dept. of Veterans Affairs
programs.eligibility: Veteran with a service-connected evaluation of at least 80%, OR receiving VA compensation at the 100% rate. Must own and occupy a Washington primary residence and meet the combined disposable income limit. VA disability compensation and DIC are NOT counted as income. The income limit is the county-specific 'Income Threshold 3' (varies by county).
programs.coverage: Reduces property taxes via a tiered exemption: at lower income tiers the home value is partially exempted and the residence is exempt from all excess (voter-approved) levies, with greater exemptions at lower income. Exact exemption amount and income thresholds are set per county — verify with your county assessor.
programs.notes: Same program covers seniors (61+), people retired due to disability, and disabled veterans. RCW 84.36.381. Apply through your county assessor.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran (DAV) License Plate & Vehicle Fee Exemption
programs.agency: Washington State Department of Licensing (DOL); eligibility via WA Dept. of Veterans Affairs
programs.eligibility: Veteran rated by the VA/military at the 100% service-connected rate expected to last more than one year, OR who lost the use of both hands or one foot, or became blind in both eyes from military service. Vehicle must be for personal use (not registered to a business).
programs.coverage: Exempt from vehicle license (registration) fees on one vehicle per year. Plates are valid for the life of the veteran.
programs.notes: Authority RCW 46.18.235. DOL Special Plate Unit: 360-902-3770.

programs.name: Veterans' Reduced-Fee Hunting & Fishing Licenses
programs.agency: Washington Department of Fish & Wildlife (WDFW)
programs.eligibility: Resident veterans with at least a 30% service-connected disability (verified by VA letter), OR resident veterans age 65+ with any service-connected disability. Non-resident veterans meeting the same criteria also qualify. Honorable discharge required.
programs.coverage: Residents: combination fishing license at the reduced rate of $5; hunting licenses at the youth hunting fee rate (RCW 77.32.480). Non-residents: licenses issued at the resident price instead of the higher non-resident price.
programs.notes: Reduced fees apply to licenses only. Apply by mailing the reduced-fee application plus VA rating letter to WDFW Licensing Division, Olympia.

programs.name: Washington State Veterans Homes
programs.agency: Washington State Department of Veterans Affairs (WDVA)
programs.eligibility: Applicant must need nursing-home level care; have served at any time in any branch of the U.S. Armed Forces with an honorable discharge (or otherwise qualify for federal VA benefits); and reside in Washington State. Spouses of current residents, widows/widowers of eligible veterans, and Gold Star Parents are also eligible.
programs.coverage: Four Medicare/Medicaid-certified homes providing 24-hour skilled nursing care plus therapies and hospice: Washington Soldiers Home (Orting), Washington Veterans Home (Retsil/Port Orchard), Spokane Veterans Home, and Walla Walla Veterans Home. Veterans rated 70–100% service-connected may have care paid by the VA; homes also accept Medicare, Medicaid, insurance, and private pay.
programs.notes: Toll-free admissions line: 1-877-838-7787.

programs.name: State Income Tax on Military Retired Pay (None)
programs.agency: Washington State Department of Revenue (DOR)
programs.eligibility: All Washington residents, including military retirees.
programs.coverage: Washington has NO personal/individual income tax, so military retired pay (and active-duty pay, VA disability compensation, and TSP distributions) is 100% exempt from state income tax.
programs.notes: One of the states with no personal income tax; no state-level deduction form is needed because no individual income tax exists.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran Property Tax Exemption (Prop 130)
programs.agency: County Assessors (per A.R.S. § 42-11111; authorized by Prop 130, 2022)
programs.eligibility: Arizona-resident veteran with a VA service-connected disability rating; the exemption is prorated by the VA disability percentage. Subject to household income and assessed-value caps. Surviving spouses and certain disabled persons may also qualify. Apply through the county assessor.
programs.coverage: 2026: up to $4,873 of assessed (Limited Property) value, multiplied by the VA disability rating (e.g., a 60% rating = $2,924). Property assessed value may not exceed $36,454; qualifying household income may not exceed $39,865 (or $47,826 with minor children). Amounts are indexed annually.
programs.notes: Prop 130 (2022) restored constitutional authority for the veteran exemption; the operative statute is A.R.S. § 42-11111. It is an assessed-value exemption on a primary residence. Confirm the current year's figures with your county assessor.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran (DV) License Plate & VLT/Registration Fee Exemption
programs.agency: Arizona Department of Transportation, Motor Vehicle Division (ADOT MVD)
programs.eligibility: Veteran certified as 100% disabled by the VA (including those rated less than 100% but compensated at the 100% rate due to individual unemployability). Surviving spouses qualify until remarriage, with annual recertification.
programs.coverage: Full waiver of Vehicle License Tax (VLT) and registration/public-safety fees on one vehicle (transferable to a replacement vehicle). VLT varies by vehicle value/age, so this is a 100% waiver rather than a fixed dollar amount.
programs.notes: The VLT exemption must be processed in person or by mail at an MVD or authorized Third Party office with VA certification — not through the online portal. Statutory basis A.R.S. § 28-5802.

programs.name: Complimentary Disabled Veteran's Hunting & Fishing License
programs.agency: Arizona Game and Fish Department (AZGFD)
programs.eligibility: Resident veteran with VA certification of permanent 100% service-connected disability who has been a bona fide Arizona resident for at least one consecutive year.
programs.coverage: Complimentary (free) license granting all privileges of the Combination Hunting & Fishing License plus the Urban Fishing License (paper license free; a plastic card costs $4). Additional stamps/tags purchased separately.
programs.notes: If the VA letter states the 100% rating is permanent and won't be re-evaluated, the license is valid for life; otherwise it expires three years from issuance. Apply at an AZGFD office or by mail with the VA benefits letter.

programs.name: Arizona State Veteran Homes
programs.agency: Arizona Department of Veterans' Services (ADVS)
programs.eligibility: Honorably-separated veteran (or the spouse of a veteran) who requires skilled nursing care as determined by a physician, with documented absence of tuberculosis. Admission arranged through each home's Admissions Coordinator.
programs.coverage: Skilled nursing / long-term care at four state homes: Phoenix, Tucson, Flagstaff (opened fall 2024), and Yuma. Cost is offset by VA per-diem payments; the resident pays remaining care costs based on income/benefits.
programs.notes: Four homes total as of 2026. ADVS site WAF-blocks scripted fetch; locations and eligibility confirmed via cached official pages and the NASVH directory.

programs.name: State Income Tax on Military Retired Pay (Exempt)
programs.agency: Arizona Department of Revenue (ADOR)
programs.eligibility: Any recipient of benefits, annuities, and pensions received as retired or retainer pay of the U.S. uniformed services. Both spouses may each claim if each receives such pay.
programs.coverage: 100% of military retired/retainer pay is subtracted from Arizona adjusted gross income (fully exempt). No dollar cap.
programs.notes: Effective for tax years 2021 onward (prior caps were $2,500, then $3,500). Applies to military retired pay, not VA disability compensation (which is federally tax-exempt regardless).

programs.name: Property Tax Relief for Disabled Veterans
programs.agency: Tennessee Comptroller of the Treasury (administered through your County Trustee's office)
programs.eligibility: Tennessee homeowner who owns and occupies the property as a primary residence and is a disabled veteran meeting one of: service-connected paraplegia/permanent paralysis of both legs, loss/loss of use of two or more limbs, or legal blindness; service-connected permanent and total (100%) disability per the VA; or 100% total and permanent disability from being a prisoner of war. Unremarried surviving spouses may also qualify. No income limit for the veteran benefit.
programs.coverage: The state reimburses property tax on the first $175,000 of the home's full market value (per T.C.A. § 67-5-704).
programs.notes: Apply through your County Trustee's office. The largest single state-funded veterans benefit in Tennessee.

programs.name: Free Disabled Veteran License Plate
programs.agency: Tennessee Department of Revenue (Vehicle Services)
programs.eligibility: Veteran with a VA letter verifying a permanent and total (100%) service-connected disability rating, or otherwise entitled to VA compensation for disabilities incurred in/aggravated by active service. VA documentation required.
programs.coverage: First plate is free (no registration fee). A second plate costs $26.50 annually. Veterans grandfathered before May 19, 2014 may receive two free plates. 100% permanent-and-total disabled veterans are also exempt from the motor vehicle privilege/wheel tax.
programs.notes: Apply on Form VR-13.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran Sport Hunting & Fishing License
programs.agency: Tennessee Wildlife Resources Agency (TWRA)
programs.eligibility: Tennessee resident veteran who is either 100% permanently and totally disabled from a service-connected cause, or 30% or more disabled by reason of service in any war.
programs.coverage: A one-time $10 fee for a combination sport fishing and hunting license (lifetime; not an annual renewal).
programs.notes: Apply via the TWRA Miscellaneous Licenses Application.

programs.name: Tennessee State Veterans' Homes
programs.agency: Tennessee State Veterans' Homes (TSVH) Board
programs.eligibility: Honorably discharged veteran needing skilled care who also meets at least one of: entered the U.S. Armed Forces in Tennessee; has Tennessee as official Home of Record; has an immediate-family primary caregiver who is a Tennessee resident; or is a Tennessee resident at admission. DD-214 required. Spouses and Gold Star parents eligible on a space-available basis.
programs.coverage: Skilled nursing / long-term care. Cost is offset by VA per-diem payments plus Medicare/Medicaid/private pay.
programs.notes: Locations: Murfreesboro, Humboldt, Knoxville, Clarksville, and Cleveland.

programs.name: State Income Tax on Military Retired Pay (None)
programs.agency: Tennessee Department of Revenue
programs.eligibility: All Tennessee residents, including military retirees.
programs.coverage: Tennessee imposes no state income tax on wages, salaries, or any retirement income, including military retired pay.
programs.notes: Tennessee has never taxed earned income, and the Hall income tax (on certain interest/dividends only) was fully repealed for tax years beginning on or after Jan 1, 2021.

programs.name: Property Tax Credit ('Circuit Breaker') & Former POW Homestead Exemption
programs.agency: Missouri Department of Revenue / Missouri State Tax Commission
programs.eligibility: Property Tax Credit: Missouri seniors (65+), certain disabled, and 100% disabled individuals (including 100% disabled veterans) who paid real estate tax or rent, subject to household income limits. Former POW Homestead Exemption (MO Constitution Art. X, Sec. 6): a former prisoner of war who is 100% service-connected disabled, owning and occupying a Missouri homestead (max 5 acres) as primary residence, is fully exempt from real property tax.
programs.coverage: Property Tax Credit: max $750 (renters) or $1,100 (owners), scaled by tax/rent paid and household income. Former POW homestead: 100% exemption from real property tax.
programs.notes: These are the two property-tax benefits that exist in 2026. A broad tiered disabled-veteran property tax exemption circulating online is NOT law — it is a pending constitutional amendment requiring Senate passage and November 2026 voter approval. Credit claimed on Form MO-PTC; POW exemption filed via the county assessor.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran (DV) License Plates
programs.agency: Missouri Department of Revenue, Motor Vehicle Bureau
programs.eligibility: Missouri resident honorably discharged from the U.S. Armed Forces with a service-connected disability (documented by a VA statement no more than one year old). Apply via Form 4601.
programs.coverage: One free set of DV plates — no specialty-plate, transfer, processing, or replacement fees (personalization also free). Additional sets are subject to standard fees.
programs.notes: Plates confer disabled parking only if they display the wheelchair symbol (requires a physician statement).

programs.name: Disabled Veteran / POW Free Hunting & Fishing Permit Exemption
programs.agency: Missouri Department of Conservation
programs.eligibility: Honorably discharged resident or nonresident veteran with a service-related disability of 60% or greater, OR a former prisoner of war, OR currently assigned as a patient to a Warrior Transition Brigade/Unit or military medical center. A certified VA statement must be carried.
programs.coverage: No permit required (free) to hunt small game and fish. Excludes black bears, deer, elk, and turkeys (these still require the applicable permit). Trout permit, Migratory Bird Permit, and Federal Duck Stamp still required where applicable.
programs.notes: Trapping is not covered. Other qualifying veterans may buy permits at resident prices.

programs.name: Missouri Veterans Homes (Long-Term Skilled Nursing Care)
programs.agency: Missouri Veterans Commission (MO Dept. of Public Safety)
programs.eligibility: Meet VA criteria for veteran status; be a Missouri citizen with 180 consecutive days of physical residency immediately prior to application; have physician documentation requiring 24-hour skilled nursing care; not appear on any sex offender registry; no Class A or B felony history.
programs.coverage: Seven homes statewide (Cameron, Cape Girardeau, Mexico, Mt. Vernon, St. James, St. Louis, Warrensburg), ~1,238 skilled-nursing beds. Current monthly residency rate is $2,773, adjusted each January.
programs.notes: Long-term skilled nursing care (not assisted living).

programs.name: State Income Tax on Military Retired Pay (Exempt)
programs.agency: Missouri Department of Revenue
programs.eligibility: Recipients of U.S. Armed Forces military retirement/pension income filing a Missouri return (all branches).
programs.coverage: 100% of military retirement benefits are deductible from Missouri taxable income (full exemption), claimed on Form MO-A, Part 1.
programs.notes: Fully phased in and in effect for 2026.

programs.name: Property Tax Exemption for Veterans with a Disability & Gold Star Spouses
programs.agency: Colorado Division of Veterans Affairs (applications) / Dept. of Local Affairs, Division of Property Taxation; filed with County Assessor
programs.eligibility: Veteran with a 100% permanent-and-total service-connected disability (including those rated at least 70% but paid at the 100% rate via Individual Unemployability), who served 24+ months active duty with an honorable discharge and occupies the property as primary residence since Jan 1 of the application year. Gold Star spouses also qualify; remarriage does not disqualify.
programs.coverage: Exempts 50% of the first $200,000 of actual value of the primary residence (the state reimburses the local property tax on that exempted value).
programs.notes: Application deadline is July 1, filed with the County Assessor. Same 50%/$200k structure as the senior homestead exemption.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran (D.V.) License Plate
programs.agency: Colorado Department of Revenue, Division of Motor Vehicles (verified via Colorado Division of Veterans Affairs)
programs.eligibility: Veteran rated 50% or more service-connected disabled by the VA, OR with loss of use of one/both feet or hands, OR permanent blindness in both eyes, plus proof of honorable discharge. VA qualification letter required.
programs.coverage: The first set of D.V. plates is exempt from fees under C.R.S. 42-3-213; a second/additional set carries a one-time $50.00 issuance fee plus applicable taxes and fees.
programs.notes: A separate U.S. Disabled Woman Veteran plate also exists. Apply via the County Motor Vehicle Office.

programs.name: Lifetime Fishing / Small-Game Combination License for Disabled Veterans
programs.agency: Colorado Parks and Wildlife (CPW)
programs.eligibility: Colorado residents who are military veterans with a service-connected disability rated 50% or more (combined) by the VA, or Purple Heart recipients. Valid only while Colorado residency is maintained.
programs.coverage: Free lifetime license (Lifetime Fishing, or Lifetime Fishing & Small Game Hunting Combination); holders are exempt from buying the annual Habitat Stamp.
programs.notes: Authorized by the Colorado Heroes Hunting & Fishing Act. Can serve as a qualifying license for big-game draws. Apply via a CPW account; allow ~15 business days for verification.

programs.name: Colorado Veterans Community Living Centers (VCLCs)
programs.agency: Colorado Department of Human Services (CDHS)
programs.eligibility: Honorably discharged veterans, veterans' spouses or widow(er)s, and Gold Star parents, who also meet medical/clinical criteria for long-term care or short-term rehabilitation.
programs.coverage: Long-term care and short-term rehabilitation; accepts Medicaid and private pay. VA per-diem and income/asset-based VA benefits may apply for wartime veterans and spouses/widows.
programs.notes: Five centers: Florence (Bruce McCandless), Homelake (Monte Vista), Rifle, Walsenburg, and Fitzsimons (Aurora). Secure memory-care units at Fitzsimons, Florence, Rifle, and Walsenburg.

programs.name: State Income Tax Subtraction for Military Retirement Pay
programs.agency: Colorado Department of Revenue, Division of Taxation
programs.eligibility: Retired servicemembers receiving military retirement benefits included in federal taxable income. Two tracks based on age at year-end: a military-specific subtraction for those under 55, and the general pension/annuity subtraction for those 55+.
programs.coverage: Under age 55: subtract up to $15,000 of military retirement benefits. Age 55–64: up to $20,000 via the general pension/annuity subtraction. Age 65+: up to $24,000 via the general pension/annuity subtraction.
programs.notes: Claimed on the Subtractions from Income Schedule (DR 0104AD). The $20k/$24k pension caps are shared across all qualifying retirement income, not military-only. A 2025 bill to remove the caps for TY2026 was postponed indefinitely and did not become law.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran Property Tax Exemption (Dwelling House)
programs.agency: Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT), via local county assessment offices
programs.eligibility: Veteran whom the VA has determined to have a 100% service-connected, permanent and total disability; applies to the veteran's principal dwelling. Also available to disabled active-duty service members, certain unremarried surviving spouses of qualifying disabled veterans, and surviving spouses of service members killed in the line of duty.
programs.coverage: 100% (full) exemption from real property tax on the dwelling house and surrounding yard/curtilage. Retroactive refunds available up to 3 years when the exemption was authorized but not yet granted.
programs.notes: Statutory basis MD Tax-Property Article 7-208. Surviving spouses must generally remain unremarried. Apply to the local county office with DD-214 and the most recent VA rating notification.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran / Veteran License Plates & Registration Fee Waiver
programs.agency: Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA)
programs.eligibility: Veterans with a VA service-connected disability rating. DV plates issued to those rated 50–99% (recognition plates) and to those rated 100%/totally and permanently disabled. Apply via Form VR-120 with VA documentation.
programs.coverage: Veterans rated 100% service-connected: plates issued free and annual registration fees waived. Veterans rated 50–99%: plates issued free, but annual registration fee and surcharge still apply. The $25 organizational plate fee is waived for disabled veterans rated over 50% and Gold Star families.

programs.name: Complimentary Lifetime Hunting & Fishing License (Disabled Veterans / Former POWs)
programs.agency: Maryland Department of Natural Resources (DNR)
programs.eligibility: Maryland residents who are 100% service-connected disabled veterans, former prisoners of war, or deemed unemployable by the VA. Present a VA letter and completed application in person at a DNR Licensing and Registration Service Center.
programs.coverage: Free (complimentary) lifetime license. Hunting license includes lifetime archery, muzzleloader, and sika deer stamps and a furbearer permit (excludes the annual MD Migratory Game Bird Stamp). Fishing license includes the non-tidal angler's license, trout stamp, Chesapeake Bay sport fishing license, and recreational oyster license.
programs.notes: Available only at DNR service centers (not online). DNR customer service: 866-344-8889.

programs.name: Charlotte Hall Veterans Home
programs.agency: Maryland Department of Veterans and Military Families (DVMF), operated with PruittHealth
programs.eligibility: Maryland veteran who served full-time active duty (other than for training) and was discharged under honorable conditions; at least 62 years old OR deemed disabled by SSA or the VA; and meets Maryland residency requirements.
programs.coverage: Cost varies by the veteran's income and service-connected disability rating; all residents receive a VA per-diem subsidy. A veteran rated 70% or greater service-connected may be entitled to the full cost of nursing home care. A continuum of care: 126-bed assisted living, 318-bed skilled nursing, and secure memory care in St. Mary's County.
programs.notes: Apply via the on-site Veterans Service Officer: 301-884-8171 ext. 5112.

programs.name: Military Retirement Income Tax Subtraction
programs.agency: Comptroller of Maryland (administered) / Maryland Dept. of Veterans and Military Families (guidance)
programs.eligibility: Individuals receiving military retirement income from qualifying U.S. Armed Forces service. Claimed on Maryland Form 502.
programs.coverage: Up to $20,000 of military retirement income subtracted if the taxpayer is at least 55 on the last day of the tax year; up to $12,500 if under age 55 (the currently enacted 'Keep Our Heroes Home Act' amounts, in effect for tax year 2026).
programs.notes: Verify the current figures on veterans.maryland.gov before relying on them: a $40,000 increase has been proposed several times (2025 HB60/SB99; 2026 HB761) but has not become law as of this writing — the enacted amounts remain $12,500/$20,000.

programs.name: Property Tax Exemption for Disabled Veterans (Homestead)
programs.agency: South Carolina Department of Revenue (SCDOR)
programs.eligibility: Veterans with a total, permanent, and service-connected disability (VA P&T rating). A 2024 expansion allows veterans who are service-connected disabled but not totally/permanently disabled to claim a partial exemption equal to their disability percentage. Surviving spouses may claim it.
programs.coverage: 100% exemption on the primary residence plus up to 5 acres of land, and on up to 2 private passenger vehicles. Retroactive claims allowed for up to the prior two years if taxes were paid on time.
programs.notes: Apply via MyDORWAY. Exemption begins the year disability occurs or property is acquired, whichever is later.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran License Plate & Vehicle Property Tax Exemption
programs.agency: South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) / SCDOR
programs.eligibility: DV plate: veteran VA-certified for loss of use of legs/arms, virtual blindness in both eyes, or total and permanent disability; requires VA documentation or SCDVA certification of a combat-related disability and honorable discharge. Vehicle property tax exemption: total/permanent service-connected disabled veterans.
programs.coverage: The DV license plate is free (three free sets provided). The vehicle property tax exemption covers up to 2 private passenger vehicles. Military plates issued after May 6, 2022 also include free parking at SC metered spaces.
programs.notes: Vehicle property tax exemption applied via SCDOR MyDORWAY.

programs.name: Free Hunting & Fishing Disability License
programs.agency: South Carolina Department of Natural Resources (SCDNR)
programs.eligibility: South Carolina resident veterans with a service-connected disability (current disability certification dated within the past 12 months required).
programs.coverage: Free 3-year Disability Combination License covering freshwater fishing, saltwater fishing, state hunting, big game, Wildlife Management Areas, and the Migratory Waterfowl Permit; includes the base set of deer tags each year.
programs.notes: Apply at the SCDNR 'Disabled' license page or via DisabilityLicense@dnr.sc.gov / 803-734-3838.

programs.name: State Veterans Nursing Homes
programs.agency: South Carolina Department of Veterans' Affairs (SCDVA)
programs.eligibility: Veterans separated under general or honorable conditions, who are South Carolina residents, and who need skilled or intermediate nursing home care. Apply through a county Veterans' Affairs officer or directly with a facility.
programs.coverage: Six state veterans homes: E. Roy Stone Veterans Pavilion (Columbia), Veterans' Victory House (Walterboro), Richard Michael Campbell Veterans Home (Anderson), Veteran Village (Florence), Palmetto Patriots Home (Gaffney), and Patriot's Village (Sumter). Cost is offset by VA per-diem and resident contribution.
programs.notes: Admission via the SCDVA State Home Admission Packet.

programs.name: State Income Tax on Military Retired Pay (Exempt)
programs.agency: South Carolina Department of Revenue (SCDOR)
programs.eligibility: All military retirees with military retirement income included in SC taxable income, regardless of age. Also claimable by a surviving spouse receiving military retirement income.
programs.coverage: 100% of military retirement income is deductible from SC taxable income (full exemption, no age limit and no earned-income cap).
programs.notes: Effective for tax years 2022 onward under the Workforce Enhancement and Military Recognition Act.

programs.name: Homestead Exemption for Permanently & Totally Disabled Persons
programs.agency: Alabama Department of Revenue (administered by local county taxing officials)
programs.eligibility: Any taxpayer who is permanently and totally disabled, regardless of age or income. A 100% permanently and totally disabled veteran qualifies under this category (the statute is disability-based, not veteran-specific). Proof via VA pension/annuity award or Physician's Affidavit. Apply through the local county taxing official.
programs.coverage: 100% exemption from all ad valorem (property) taxes (state, county, and municipal) on the principal residence. No assessed-value cap and no income limit; homestead limited to an owner-occupied dwelling and land not exceeding 160 acres.
programs.notes: Alabama has no dedicated 'disabled veteran' property-tax statute; a 100% P&T-rated veteran qualifies through the general disabled (H-3) homestead exemption.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran License Plate & Registration Fee Exemption
programs.agency: Alabama Department of Revenue, Motor Vehicle Division
programs.eligibility: Alabama resident who is a service-connected disabled veteran. Documentation: VA disability rating certification plus military ID, DD-214, or VA affidavit.
programs.coverage: 10%–50% rating: first plate exempt from registration and issuance fees (ad valorem tax still owed). 51%+ rating (or vehicle with special mechanical controls): first plate exempt from registration and issuance fees, $5 annual fee on additional plates. Vehicle funded by the VA: all plates exempt from registration fees AND ad valorem taxes.
programs.notes: Statutory basis Code of Ala. § 40-12-254 / § 40-12-271.1.

programs.name: Military Veteran's Appreciation Hunting & Fishing Licenses (Disabled Veterans)
programs.agency: Alabama Department of Conservation and Natural Resources (Outdoor Alabama)
programs.eligibility: Resident veterans certified by the VA. Hunting: minimum 50% disability (or 100% disabled). Freshwater fishing: minimum 20% disability. Saltwater: 20%+ disability eligible for a reduced-rate annual license. Show a VA disability-rating letter; obtain at the local probate office or by mail from DCNR.
programs.coverage: Reduced-cost (not free). Annual disabled-veteran freshwater license: $2 license fee + $1 issuance fee. Lifetime disabled-veteran freshwater fishing license: $45 (under 50) / $25 (50+). Alabama residents 65+ are exempt from buying recreational hunting/fishing/WMA licenses and the state duck stamp.
programs.notes: These veteran licenses are reduced-rate, not free.

programs.name: Alabama State Veterans Homes
programs.agency: Alabama Department of Veterans Affairs (ADVA)
programs.eligibility: Honorably discharged with a minimum of 90 continuous days of active duty service (post-1980/1981 enlistees/commissionees must have 24 continuous months or the full period called); Alabama resident for the immediate past 12 months; meets VA criteria for skilled nursing (or assisted living) care; passes a background check.
programs.coverage: A monthly residency fee applies (set per facility). Veterans with a 70%+ service-connected disability rating, or admitted for a service-connected condition, may have costs covered by the VA.
programs.notes: Five ADVA homes: Bill Nichols (Alexander City), William F. Green (Bay Minette), Floyd E. 'Tut' Fann (Huntsville), Colonel Robert L. Howard (Pell City), and CSM Bennie G. Adkins (Enterprise).

programs.name: State Income Tax on Military Retired Pay (Exempt)
programs.agency: Alabama Department of Revenue
programs.eligibility: All retired military personnel receiving military retirement pay. No age requirement and no income cap.
programs.coverage: 100% exempt. Military retirement pay is fully exempt from Alabama state income tax (also exempt from county/municipal income tax). SBP/RCSBP survivor annuities are likewise exempt.
programs.notes: Statutory basis Code of Ala. § 40-18-20; full exemption effective Jan 1, 1989.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran Property Tax Relief
programs.agency: Indiana Department of Veterans Affairs / county auditor
programs.eligibility: Honorably discharged veteran, at least 90 days active duty, AND either rated 100% disabled / Individual Unemployability, OR age 62+ with a 10%+ service-connected disability, OR (wartime-service track) a 10%+ service-connected disability. Surviving spouses may retain eligibility.
programs.coverage: Through taxes payable 2026: a $14,000 assessed-value deduction (totally disabled / 62+ partial, $200,000 value cap) and/or a $24,960 assessed-value deduction (wartime service, 10%+, no cap), which can stack. Indiana's House Enrolled Act 1210 (2026) restructures this for the 2026 assessment date / taxes payable 2027 — totally disabled (100%/IU) veterans move to a full homestead exemption (no value cap), and the wartime/partial deduction becomes local credits.
programs.notes: The official DVA property-tax page is mid-update for the new law. Confirm the current year's amounts and whether you register with the county auditor before relying on a specific figure.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran / Veteran License Plates
programs.agency: Indiana Bureau of Motor Vehicles (BMV) / Indiana DVA
programs.eligibility: Indiana resident veterans. The Disabled Veteran (DV) plate requires a qualifying service-connected disability certified by the VA; other designation plates (Military Branch, Purple Heart, Ex-POW) are available to qualifying veterans.
programs.coverage: Indiana offers a Disabled Veteran (DV) plate plus multiple veteran/military designation plates. Confirm the current excise-tax exemption and any plate fee directly with the Indiana BMV.
programs.notes: Exact excise-tax/registration fee figures are not published on the DVA services page — verify with the BMV before relying on a dollar amount.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran Discounted Hunting & Fishing License
programs.agency: Indiana Department of Natural Resources (DNR) / Indiana DVA
programs.eligibility: Indiana resident who served in the U.S. Armed Forces and has a documented service-connected disability per the VA (or DoD disability retirement). No minimum rating percentage. Requires DVA certification before first purchase (State Form 50833).
programs.coverage: $2.75 per year, or $27.50 for a 10-year license. Covers small-game hunting and fishing; excludes stamps (waterfowl, game bird, trout/salmon) and does not cover deer or turkey. A separate Golden Hoosier Passport ($25/year) gives unlimited state-park admission.
programs.notes: Catastrophically disabled resident veterans may also hunt license/stamp-free on a few designated free-hunting days each year.

programs.name: Indiana Veterans' Home (West Lafayette)
programs.agency: Indiana Veterans' Home (state agency)
programs.eligibility: Honorably discharged Indiana veterans and their spouses; Gold Star parents also eligible. Located in West Lafayette. Generally requires Indiana residency.
programs.coverage: Long-term skilled nursing care, short-term rehabilitation, and memory care. A means-based resident fee applies, offset by VA per-diem and other benefits.
programs.notes: Confirm exact residency-duration and fee specifics with IVH (765-463-1502).

programs.name: State Income Tax on Military Retired Pay (Exempt)
programs.agency: Indiana Department of Revenue (DOR)
programs.eligibility: Any Indiana resident reporting military retirement income and/or survivor's benefits, regardless of age.
programs.coverage: 100% deduction with no dollar limit — military retirement pay and survivor's benefits are fully exempt from Indiana adjusted gross income tax (effective tax year 2022 onward).
programs.notes: Claimed on Form IT-40 in the Military Retirement and/or Survivor's Benefits Deduction line.

programs.name: Homestead / Disability Property Tax Exemption (65+ or Totally Disabled)
programs.agency: Kentucky Department of Revenue / local PVA
programs.eligibility: Kentucky homeowners age 65+ OR classified as totally and permanently disabled under a U.S. government agency or Kentucky retirement program. Veterans with a service-connected total disability qualify under the disability category and, unlike other disabled applicants, do not have to reapply annually.
programs.coverage: $49,100 deducted from assessed value for the 2025–2026 assessment period (inflation-adjusted every two years).
programs.notes: This is the general homestead/disability exemption, not veteran-specific; a disabled veteran uses the same exemption available to any totally disabled homeowner. Kentucky has no enacted veteran-specific 100% property exemption (a 2025 bill proposing one did not pass).

programs.name: Disabled Veteran License Plate
programs.agency: Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (DRIVE) / County Clerk
programs.eligibility: Honorably discharged veteran with a VA service-connected disability rating of 100% (or who received VA funds to purchase/modify a vehicle) qualifies for the no-fee plate. Veterans rated 50–99% qualify for a fee-based disabled veteran plate. Apply at the local County Clerk using Application TC 96-217 with VA certification.
programs.coverage: 100% / VA-vehicle: no-fee (free) Disabled Veteran plate. 50–99%: fee-based plate at $26 (initial and renewal).
programs.notes: Confirm the exact fee at the County Clerk. KY Dept. of Veterans Affairs: 800-572-6245.

programs.name: Disabled Sportsman's Hunting & Fishing License (Disabled Veterans)
programs.agency: Kentucky Department of Fish & Wildlife Resources
programs.eligibility: Kentucky resident veterans with at least a 50% service-connected disability rating from the VA. Requires a VA letter verifying 50%+ service-connected disability with a current KY address.
programs.coverage: $12 annually (reduced, not free). Includes the Combination Hunting & Fishing License, all Deer Permits, Spring and Fall Turkey Permits, the Migratory Bird/Waterfowl Permit, and Trout Permit.
programs.notes: Must renew annually. Federal Duck Stamp and the annual HIP survey still required separately for waterfowl.

programs.name: State Veterans Centers (Nursing Care)
programs.agency: Kentucky Department of Veterans Affairs
programs.eligibility: Veteran with a discharge that is not dishonorable, a Kentucky resident as of the date of admission, disabled by disease, wounds, age, or otherwise in need of nursing care. Admission is based on nursing-care need and urgency (service-connected status does not grant priority).
programs.coverage: Four state-operated skilled-nursing veterans centers: Thomson-Hood (Wilmore), Paul E. Patton Eastern Kentucky Veterans Center (Hazard), Joseph 'Eddie' Ballard Western Kentucky Veterans Center (Hanson), and Carl M. Brashear Radcliff Veterans Center (Radcliff).
programs.notes: Admissions contact: KDVA (502) 595-4447.

programs.name: State Income Tax on Military Retired Pay (Partial / Date-Based)
programs.agency: Kentucky Department of Revenue
programs.eligibility: All Kentucky taxpayers receiving military retired pay. Treatment depends on retirement date relative to January 1, 1998.
programs.coverage: Military retired pay attributable to service BEFORE Jan 1, 1998 is 100% exempt. Pay attributable to service AFTER Dec 31, 1997 is covered by Kentucky's general pension income exclusion of up to $31,110. Members with service both before and after 1998 compute an exempt percentage on Schedule P and may exclude more than $31,110.
programs.notes: The $31,110 general pension exclusion is shared across retirement income, not military-only.

programs.name: Wisconsin Veterans & Surviving Spouses Property Tax Credit
