programs.agency: Wisconsin Department of Revenue (administers) / Wisconsin Department of Veterans Affairs (certifies)
programs.eligibility: Veteran with a 100% service-connected disability rating OR a 100% rating based on individual unemployability. Must have entered active duty as a Wisconsin resident or been a WI resident for any consecutive 5-year period after entering service, and currently reside in WI; honorable discharge. Unremarried surviving spouses receiving DIC may also qualify. WDVA verification must accompany the first-year return.
programs.coverage: A refundable credit equal to 100% of the property taxes paid during the year on the eligible principal dwelling.
programs.notes: Claimed as a refundable credit on the Wisconsin state income tax return — the veteran pays the property tax and is reimbursed through the return; it is not a direct property-tax exemption.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran (DV) Parking License Plates
programs.agency: Wisconsin Department of Transportation (DMV)
programs.eligibility: Wisconsin veteran certified by an authorized VA health care specialist as having a permanent disability incurred during active military service that limits or impairs the ability to walk. Vehicle must be titled to the disabled veteran.
programs.coverage: Standard annual vehicle registration fee applies; an additional $15/year only if personalized plates are chosen. There is no statewide registration-fee waiver for these plates.
programs.notes: These are mobility/parking-privilege plates; Wisconsin does not waive the annual registration fee for the DV parking plate.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran Hunting & Fishing Privileges
programs.agency: Wisconsin Department of Natural Resources (DNR)
programs.eligibility: Resident Disabled Veteran Recreation Card: service-connected disability rating of 50% or greater, or individually unemployable. Resident Disabled Veteran Fishing License: service-connected rating of 70% or greater, or individually unemployable. Documentation required at purchase.
programs.coverage: Disabled Veteran Recreation Card: $7/year (includes fishing, small game, state park vehicle admission, and a state trail pass). Disabled Veteran Fishing License: $3/year (fishing only). Reduced Spring Turkey harvest authorization: $10.
programs.notes: The $7 Recreation Card (50%+ rating) is the broader bundle; the $3 fishing-only license has a higher 70% threshold.

programs.name: Wisconsin Veterans Homes (King, Union Grove, Chippewa Falls)
programs.agency: Wisconsin Department of Veterans Affairs (WDVA)
programs.eligibility: Veteran who served on active duty during wartime for at least 90 days (one day during a wartime period), OR served 2+ years (or full initial obligation) during peacetime; honorable discharge. Spouses of veterans and Gold Star Parents are also eligible. Wisconsin residency is NOT required, but WI residents of 6+ continuous months receive first admission priority.
programs.coverage: 24-hour skilled nursing care at three homes (Chippewa Falls, King, Union Grove). Members able to pay are billed monthly for cost of care; those unable to pay may qualify for Medicare or Medicaid.
programs.notes: Detailed homes site: wisvetshomes.com.

programs.name: State Income Tax on Military Retired Pay (Exempt)
programs.agency: Wisconsin Department of Revenue
programs.eligibility: Recipients of U.S. military retirement pay (including Retired Serviceman's Family Protection Plan and Survivor Benefit Plan payments), plus Coast Guard, NOAA, and Public Health Service commissioned corps.
programs.coverage: 100% exempt from Wisconsin state income tax. No income limit, no age requirement, and no dollar cap.
programs.notes: Claimed as a subtraction from income on Schedule SB (Form 1) or Schedule M (Form 1NPR).

programs.name: Market Value Exclusion for Veterans with a Disability
programs.agency: Minnesota Department of Revenue (administered by county assessors)
programs.eligibility: Honorably discharged veteran who owns and occupies a Minnesota homestead with a VA service-connected disability rating of 70% or higher. Surviving spouses receiving dependency and indemnity compensation, and primary family caregivers, may also qualify. Apply to the county assessor by Dec 31.
programs.coverage: $150,000 market value exclusion for a 70%+ service-connected disability; $300,000 exclusion for 100% permanent and total (or permanent Individual Unemployability). Surviving spouses of 100% P&T veterans may continue the $300,000 exclusion until remarriage or property transfer.
programs.notes: Reduces the taxable market value of the homestead. Work with a County Veterans Service Officer; the caregiver exclusion matches the veteran's tier.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran Vehicle Fee Exemption & Veteran License Plates
programs.agency: Minnesota Department of Public Safety — Driver and Vehicle Services (DVS)
programs.eligibility: Veterans with a 100% total and permanent service-connected disability rating or a VA Individual Unemployability rating qualify for full registration/title/plate fee and sales-tax exemption. A range of military and veteran specialty plates are available to eligible veterans more broadly.
programs.coverage: Free motor vehicle registration, plate, and title services for up to two vehicles for 100%/TDIU disabled veterans (fee exemption effective Jan 1, 2024; sales-tax exemption effective July 1, 2024). Plates can include the disability parking symbol for qualified applicants.
programs.notes: The exemption does not cover personalized-plate fees or required specialty-plate contributions.

programs.name: Hunting & Fishing Licenses for Disabled Veterans
programs.agency: Minnesota Department of Natural Resources (DNR)
programs.eligibility: Resident veterans. 100% permanently and totally disabled veterans (including TDIU) qualify for a free permanent angling license and a 100% Disabled Veteran license card (priority in bear and deer lotteries). Veterans with a 50–99% service-connected disability qualify for reduced-fee deer, small game, and angling licenses.
programs.coverage: Free permanent angling license for 100% P&T disabled veterans. For 50–99% service-connected disabled veterans, a $5 reduced rate applies to deer, small game, and angling licenses — but this $5 rate takes effect March 1, 2027; until then 50–99% veterans pay standard fees.
programs.notes: Apply through the DNR License Center (888-646-6367). The $5 reduced fee for 50–99% veterans is enacted but not yet in effect as of June 2026.

programs.name: Minnesota Veterans Homes (Skilled Nursing / Long-Term Care)
programs.agency: Minnesota Department of Veterans Affairs (MDVA)
programs.eligibility: Veterans discharged under honorable conditions who are current Minnesota residents and served 181 consecutive days of active duty (unless discharged earlier for a line-of-duty disability) and require skilled nursing care. Spouses of eligible veterans may apply if at least 55 and meeting residency requirements.
programs.coverage: Eight state Veterans Homes: Bemidji, Fergus Falls, Hastings, Luverne, Minneapolis, Montevideo, Preston, and Silver Bay. Skilled nursing, dementia/Alzheimer's special care, domiciliary care, and rehabilitation. Residents contribute to the cost of care according to their means.
programs.notes: Bemidji, Montevideo, and Preston are newer additions to the original five.

programs.name: Military Retirement Pay Subtraction
programs.agency: Minnesota Department of Revenue
programs.eligibility: Taxpayers receiving federally taxable military retirement pay, including active-component and reserve-component retirement and Survivor Benefit Plan (SBP) payments. Pensions solely from dual-status technician service do not qualify.
programs.coverage: 100% of qualifying military retirement pay may be subtracted from Minnesota taxable income — no dollar cap or age limit.
programs.notes: Claimed on Schedule M1M. Cannot be combined with the Credit for Past Military Service; choose whichever gives the greater benefit.

programs.name: 100% Disabled Veterans Real Property Tax Exemption (Homestead)
programs.agency: Oklahoma Tax Commission / county assessor (registration via Oklahoma Department of Veterans Affairs)
programs.eligibility: Honorably-discharged Oklahoma resident veteran (or Oklahoma National Guard) certified by the VA as 100% permanent, service-connected disabled; must own and occupy the homestead as primary residence on January 1. Unremarried surviving spouse may also qualify.
programs.coverage: 100% of the fair cash value of the homestead (full property tax exemption; no dollar cap).
programs.notes: Apply with OTC Form 998 plus VA certification to the local county assessor. First enroll in the Oklahoma Veterans Registry through ODVA (888-655-2838).

programs.name: 100% DAV Sales Tax Exemption & DAV License Plate / Reduced Registration
programs.agency: Oklahoma Tax Commission (sales tax) and Service Oklahoma (license plate / registration)
programs.eligibility: Oklahoma resident veteran certified by the VA as receiving compensation at the 100% rate for a permanent, service-connected disability. Unremarried surviving spouse may also qualify at a reduced limit.
programs.coverage: Sales tax exemption on qualifying purchases up to $25,000 per year (surviving spouse: $1,000 per year); a DAV specialty license plate with a $5 flat annual registration fee.
programs.notes: Register with the Oklahoma Veterans Registry at ODVA to obtain Form 599.

programs.name: Resident Disabled Veteran Hunting & Fishing License
programs.agency: Oklahoma Department of Wildlife Conservation (ODWC)
programs.eligibility: Legal Oklahoma resident veterans disabled as certified by the VA. The license-purchase exemption requires a 60%+ VA disability rating; the deer-license exemption requires a 100% rating.
programs.coverage: Free (exempt from purchasing) annual hunting and fishing licenses at 60%+ disability, plus exemption from deer licenses at 100%. Discounted lifetime combination license: $25 (60%+ disability) or $200 (under 60%).
programs.notes: Obtain proof of exemption through ODVA (888-655-2838).

programs.name: Oklahoma Veterans Centers (State Veterans Homes)
programs.agency: Oklahoma Department of Veterans Affairs (ODVA)
programs.eligibility: Honorable or general-under-honorable discharge; served at least 90 days with one or more days on active duty (or discharged earlier due to a service-connected disability); Oklahoma residency at application; and a clinical assessment establishing need for nursing or domiciliary care.
programs.coverage: Long-term skilled nursing, intermediate, memory, and domiciliary care; veterans with a 70%+ service-connected VA disability rating receive full cost of care. Seven homes: Ardmore, Claremore, Clinton, Lawton, Norman, Sallisaw, and Sulphur.
programs.notes: The Sallisaw home replaced the Talihina home (Talihina closed Oct 2023; Sallisaw opened June 2025).

programs.name: State Income Tax on Military Retired Pay (Exempt)
programs.agency: Oklahoma Tax Commission
programs.eligibility: Recipients of military retirement pay/pension filing Oklahoma income tax.
programs.coverage: 100% of military retirement income is exempt from Oklahoma state income tax.
programs.notes: Oklahoma fully exempts military retired pay beginning with the 2022 tax year (Senate Bill 401); prior law allowed a deduction of the greater of $10,000 or 75%.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran or Surviving Spouse Property Tax Exemption
programs.agency: Oregon Department of Revenue / county assessors (program info via ODVA)
programs.eligibility: Oregon veteran (or active-duty member) certified as 40% or more disabled by the VA, or certified annually by a licensed physician as 40%+ disabled; surviving spouses/registered domestic partners may also qualify. Must own and live in the home as primary residence. File with the county assessor between Jan 1 and Apr 1.
programs.coverage: Reduction of homestead assessed value for tax year 2026–2027: $32,512 (service-connected disability) or $27,092 (non-service-connected disability). Both amounts increase about 3% each July 1.
programs.notes: Statutory base amounts ($18,000 / $15,000 under ORS 307.250–307.283) are indexed 3%/yr. Confirm the current-year figure on the live DOR form before relying on it.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran License Plates
programs.agency: Oregon Department of Transportation — DMV (program info via ODVA)
programs.eligibility: Veteran with an honorable discharge and a VA service-connected disability rating. Apply with the DMV application plus DD-214/DD-215 and a VA letter confirming the service-connected disability. One set of plates per qualifying veteran.
programs.coverage: A one-time $15 fee for permanent vehicle registration with the disabled veteran plate; no recurring registration fee thereafter (only standard plate/replacement fees apply).
programs.notes: The plate does not grant disabled-parking privileges.

programs.name: Free Disabled Veteran Hunting & Fishing Combination License
programs.agency: Oregon Department of Fish & Wildlife (ODFW)
programs.eligibility: Oregon resident with a service-connected disability rating of at least 25% from any branch of the U.S. Armed Forces. Apply by submitting the ODFW disabled veteran license form with a copy of the most recent VA letter showing the 25%+ rating.
programs.coverage: Free resident combination license (hunting, angling, shellfish) including the Columbia River Basin/Ocean endorsement. Eligible disabled veterans may also purchase a $25 elk tag.
programs.notes: Distinct from the separate Oregon Disabilities Hunting and Fishing Permit (65%+ disability) that grants access to certain restricted ponds/docks.

programs.name: Oregon Veterans' Homes (The Dalles & Lebanon)
programs.agency: Oregon Department of Veterans' Affairs (ODVA)
programs.eligibility: A U.S. Armed Forces veteran discharged under general or honorable conditions, OR a spouse/surviving spouse, OR a Gold Star Parent. Must need skilled or intermediate nursing care, be able to pay the resident's portion of cost, and not require care the home is not equipped to provide.
programs.coverage: Long-term skilled/intermediate nursing care. Residents may combine private pay, federal benefits, and Medicare/Medicaid. If a VA physician certifies nursing care is needed due to a service-connected disability, the VA may cover some or all of the cost.
programs.notes: Two homes: The Dalles and Lebanon. Contact ODVA 800-692-9666.

programs.name: State Income Tax Subtraction for Military Retired Pay (Pre-Oct 1991)
programs.agency: Oregon Department of Revenue (program info via ODVA)
programs.eligibility: Recipients of federal/military retired pay. The subtraction applies only to retired pay attributable to service before October 1, 1991.
programs.coverage: Subtract 100% of taxable federal pension if all service was before Oct 1, 1991; 0% if all service was on/after that date; for mixed service, a pro-rata percentage (months/points before Oct 1, 1991 divided by total).
programs.notes: Oregon has no separate blanket military-retirement exemption beyond this pre-Oct-1991 federal pension subtraction. Claimed on Oregon Schedule OR-ASC.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran Property Tax Exemption (Additional Homestead Tiers)
programs.agency: Louisiana Department of Veterans Affairs / Local Parish Assessors
programs.eligibility: Louisiana homeowner with a VA service-connected disability rating, occupying the property as primary residence; surviving spouse remains eligible while occupying and owning the home. Tiers per Constitutional Amendment No. 2 (2022), effective Jan 1, 2023.
programs.coverage: On top of the standard homestead exemption ($7,500 assessed value / $75,000 fair market value): a 50–69% rating exempts the next $2,500 of assessed value; 70–99% exempts the next $4,500; 100% exempts all remaining ad valorem taxation on the homestead (except certain municipal assessments).
programs.notes: Amounts are assessed-value exemptions. Administered by each parish assessor.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran / Military Honor License Plates
programs.agency: Louisiana Office of Motor Vehicles (OMV)
programs.eligibility: Resident veterans with a VA service-connected disability rating of 50% or more qualify for a free Disabled Veteran plate; veterans rated 100% qualify for the '100% DAV' plate. Also eligible for a free disabled-veteran hang tag and exemption from Class D/E and CDL driver-license fees.
programs.coverage: $0 — no fee for the plate and no renewal registration fee. Other purchasable veteran specialty plates (e.g., 'Support Our Veterans') cost $25.
programs.notes: OMV waived fees for several military honor plates (announced Feb 2024). Statutory basis La. R.S. 47:490.4.

programs.name: Louisiana Disabled Veteran Hunting & Fishing License
programs.agency: Louisiana Department of Wildlife and Fisheries (LDWF)
programs.eligibility: Veterans with a permanent VA service-connected disability classification of 50% or more. Available to both residents and nonresidents. Requires application plus a VA Benefit Summary Letter (or LDVA certification).
programs.coverage: Free (the Louisiana Wildlife and Fisheries Foundation covers the fee). Includes Basic and Saltwater Fishing; Basic, Deer, Waterfowl, and Turkey Hunting; and a WMA Access Permit. Does not include the Federal Duck Stamp.
programs.notes: Renewed annually. LDWF separately offers an 80%-discounted combo license for honorably discharged resident veterans (broader eligibility).

programs.name: Louisiana Veterans Homes (State Veterans Homes)
programs.agency: Louisiana Department of Veterans Affairs
programs.eligibility: Louisiana residents honorably discharged with 90 days active duty (or eligible Guard/Reservists); spouses of veterans and Gold Star parents are also eligible. Apply via the admissions/interest form to the selected home.
programs.coverage: No monthly fee for veterans with a service-connected disability rating of 70–100%; others pay below typical private nursing-home rates. Per-diem and care charges vary by income/disability.
programs.notes: Five homes: Jackson, Monroe, Bossier City, Reserve, and Jennings.

programs.name: State Income Tax on Military Retired Pay (Exempt)
programs.agency: Louisiana Department of Revenue
programs.eligibility: All recipients of federal military retirement pay (and federal civilian retirement); includes federal military Survivor Benefit Plan payments. Not age-restricted.
programs.coverage: 100% of military retirement pay is excluded from Louisiana taxable income (full exemption).
programs.notes: The exemption remained intact under Louisiana's 2025 flat 3% individual income tax reform. Separate from the general 65+ retirement-income exclusion.

programs.name: Nevada Disabled Veteran's Exemption (Property / Vehicle Tax)
programs.agency: Nevada Department of Veterans Services / County Assessors (NRS 361.091)
programs.eligibility: Nevada resident veteran with honorable discharge and a permanent service-connected disability of 60% or more. A surviving spouse who was eligible at the veteran's time of death may also qualify.
programs.coverage: Exemption of assessed valuation, tiered by disability rating (FY 2025/2026): 60–79% = $17,700; 80–99% = $26,550; 100% = $35,400. Amounts are indexed annually by CPI.
programs.notes: Filed through the County Assessor. The veteran chooses to apply the exemption to real/personal property tax OR to the Governmental Services Tax portion of DMV vehicle registration (not both).

programs.name: Veteran & Disabled Veteran License Plates
programs.agency: Nevada Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV)
programs.eligibility: Standard Veteran plate: any veteran or their spouse, parent, or child. Disabled Veteran plate: veteran with a service-connected disability rated 100% (or combined ratings totaling 100%+), with VA/DoD documentation.
programs.coverage: Disabled Veteran (and Medal of Honor, Purple Heart, POW, Gold Star) plates: $8.50 initial / $0 renewal. Standard Veteran plate: $61 initial / $30 renewal. Disabled Veteran plates also exempt the holder from state/local government parking fees.
programs.notes: Separately, the Disabled Veteran's Exemption can offset the Governmental Services Tax portion of registration via the County Assessor.

programs.name: Reduced-Fee Disabled Veteran Hunting & Fishing License
programs.agency: Nevada Department of Wildlife (NDOW), via Nevada Dept. of Veterans Services
programs.eligibility: Nevada resident veteran with a service-connected disability of 50% or more and an honorable discharge or certificate of satisfactory service. Residents only.
programs.coverage: A $15 specialty combination hunting and fishing license, valid one year from date of purchase.
programs.notes: The 50% threshold here differs from the 60% threshold for the property/vehicle tax exemption.

programs.name: Nevada State Veterans Homes (Boulder City & Sparks)
programs.agency: Nevada Department of Veterans Services
programs.eligibility: Eligible veterans (active-duty service with honorable discharge), their spouses, and Gold Star parents who require skilled nursing care. Admission begins with an application packet at veterans.nv.gov.
programs.coverage: Two homes: Southern Nevada State Veterans Home (Boulder City, 180-bed skilled nursing) and Northern Nevada State Veterans Home (Sparks/Reno). Skilled nursing, therapy, memory/dementia care, and hospice; cost offset by Medicare/Medicaid, VA per diem/pension, and private pay.
programs.notes: Southern home admissions: (702) 668-5806. Northern home: (775) 827-2955.

programs.name: State Income Tax on Military Retired Pay (None)
programs.agency: State of Nevada (no state income tax)
programs.eligibility: All Nevada residents, including military retirees.
programs.coverage: Nevada has NO state personal income tax. Military retired pay, active-duty pay, and survivor benefit annuities are entirely exempt from state income taxation.
programs.notes: One of the states with no personal income tax; no state-level taxation of any retirement or military income.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran Homestead & Personal Property Tax Exemption
programs.agency: Arkansas Assessment Coordination Division / County Collectors (Ark. Code Ann. 26-3-306)
programs.eligibility: Veteran with a VA award of special monthly compensation for loss/loss of use of one or more limbs, total blindness in one or both eyes, OR a service-connected 100% total and permanent disability rating. Unremarried surviving spouse and minor dependent children may also qualify.
programs.coverage: 100% exemption of all state taxes on the homestead and personal property owned by the qualifying disabled veteran (no dollar cap).
programs.notes: Codified at Ark. Code Ann. 26-3-306. Apply via county collector/treasurer with a VA Summary of Benefits letter.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran License Plate (Free)
programs.agency: Arkansas Department of Finance and Administration (DFA) — Office of Motor Vehicle
programs.eligibility: Service-connected disabled veteran rated 10% or greater, OR a veteran rated by the VA as 100% permanent and total non-service-connected disabled. VA verification letter required.
programs.coverage: First plate issued free of charge (no registration fee); one additional plate $4.00; surviving-spouse reissue $4.00.
programs.notes: Issued under Ark. Code 27-24-206.

programs.name: Resident Disabled Military Veteran Lifetime Hunting & Fishing Licenses
programs.agency: Arkansas Game & Fish Commission (AGFC)
programs.eligibility: 100% totally and permanently disabled with VA certification, OR a service-connected rating of 70%+, OR a service-connected rating of 50%+ with a Purple Heart. One year of Arkansas residency required.
programs.coverage: Lifetime Fishing $1.50; Lifetime Hunting $1.50; Lifetime Combination $3.00; Lifetime Combination License & Permit (incl. trout and state duck stamp) $52.50.
programs.notes: Resident-only. Federal stamps/HIP registration may still be required for migratory birds.

programs.name: Arkansas State Veterans Homes
programs.agency: Arkansas Department of Veterans Affairs (ADVA)
programs.eligibility: Honorable discharge and a medical need for nursing-home placement. Veterans, a veteran's spouse, or Gold Star parents may apply. Arkansas residents have first priority.
programs.coverage: Skilled nursing care at two homes: Fayetteville and North Little Rock. Cost is per-diem with VA per-diem offset.
programs.notes: Services include skilled nursing, hospice, therapy, and 24-hour nursing.

programs.name: State Income Tax on Military Retired Pay (Exempt)
programs.agency: Arkansas Department of Finance and Administration (DFA)
programs.eligibility: Any retired member of the uniformed services receiving military retirement benefits.
programs.coverage: 100% of military retirement / uniformed services retirement pay is exempt from Arkansas state income tax.
programs.notes: Enacted by Act 141 of 2017, effective tax year 2018; replaced the prior $6,000 retirement-income exclusion.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran Homestead Ad Valorem (Property) Tax Exemption
programs.agency: Mississippi Veterans Affairs Board (MSVA) / MS Department of Revenue (county Tax Assessor)
programs.eligibility: Honorably discharged veteran with a 100% service-connected total and permanent disability rating from the VA (also veterans 90+ years old); benefit extends to the unmarried surviving spouse.
programs.coverage: 100% exemption from all ad valorem taxes on the assessed value of the homestead.
programs.notes: Application filed at the county Tax Assessor's office Jan 1–Apr 1 each year, with a VA letter stating the 100% rating.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran License Plates (Ad Valorem & Privilege Tax Exemption)
programs.agency: Mississippi Department of Revenue / Mississippi Veterans Affairs Board
programs.eligibility: Mississippi legal resident rated 100% permanent service-connected disability, OR at least 70% nonpermanent service-connected disability, by the VA. Unmarried surviving spouse retains the benefit.
programs.coverage: $1.00 total cost per plate/tag; up to two motor vehicle tags plus one motorcycle tag. Vehicles bearing these tags are exempt from all ad valorem and privilege (road & bridge) taxes.
programs.notes: Per Miss. Code Ann. Sec. 27-19-53. Additional vehicles require standard taxes and fees.

programs.name: Hunting & Fishing License Exemption for Disabled Veterans
programs.agency: Mississippi Department of Wildlife, Fisheries, and Parks (MDWFP)
programs.eligibility: Resident veterans with a 100% total service-connected disability rating from the VA are not required to purchase a hunting or fishing license.
programs.coverage: Free — no hunting or fishing license required. An optional $5.00 Disabled Exempt License is available as a single proof-of-eligibility document.
programs.notes: Carry proof of age, residency, and the 100% service-connected disability while hunting or fishing.

programs.name: Mississippi State Veterans Homes
programs.agency: Mississippi Veterans Affairs Board (MSVA)
programs.eligibility: Must be or have been a Mississippi resident; active duty discharged under other-than-dishonorable conditions (DD-214 required); physician's exam within 30 days. Spouses of resident veterans may also qualify. Out-of-state veterans admitted only if no MS residents are waiting.
programs.coverage: No resident charge for veterans with a single service-connected rating of 70% or more, or rated 100% disabled / unemployable; assistance may be available for indigent veterans. Other residents pay a cost-of-care rate.
programs.notes: Homes located at Collins, Jackson, Kosciusko, Oxford, and Tradition/Biloxi.

programs.name: State Income Tax on Military Retired Pay (Exempt)
programs.agency: Mississippi Department of Revenue (DOR)
programs.eligibility: All recipients of military retired pay / qualified retirement income; no age or disability requirement.
programs.coverage: 100% exempt — military retired pay (and other qualified retirement income) is not subject to Mississippi income tax.
programs.notes: SBP survivor annuities and VA disability pay are also not taxed; combat-zone hazardous duty pay is exempt.

programs.name: Property Tax Relief Claim for Seniors and Disabled Veterans (K-40SVR)
programs.agency: Kansas Department of Revenue
programs.eligibility: Kansas resident the entire year who owned and occupied a Kansas home, AND is either age 65+, an honorably-discharged veteran with a service-connected disability rating of 50% or greater, or a surviving spouse of a qualifying claimant. Household income $58,041 or less (2025) and base-year home value not exceeding $350,000. Filed Jan 1 – Apr 15.
programs.coverage: Refund equal to the difference between the claimant's homestead property tax for the base year and the current year (freezes property tax at the base-year amount).
programs.notes: This is the program serving 50%+ disabled veterans (Form K-40SVR), distinct from the general Homestead Refund and the SAFESR senior program.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran License Plate
programs.agency: Kansas Department of Revenue, Division of Vehicles
programs.eligibility: Kansas resident who served in the U.S. armed forces and is entitled to compensation for a service-connected disability of at least 50%, OR has loss/permanent loss of use of one or both feet or hands, OR permanent visual impairment of both eyes. Vehicle must be titled in Kansas in the applicant's name.
programs.coverage: Initial plate: no registration fee at application or renewal (free). Additional Disabled Veteran plates: standard registration fees apply. Vehicle property tax is still due in all cases.
programs.notes: Application form is TR-103. Two plate versions exist (with/without the international wheelchair emblem).

programs.name: Disabled Veterans Hunting & Fishing License
programs.agency: Kansas Department of Wildlife and Parks (KDWP)
programs.eligibility: Any Kansas resident who is an honorably-discharged military veteran with certified service-connected disabilities of 30% or more. Must apply each year with VA entitlement papers.
programs.coverage: Free annual hunting, fishing, and hunt/fish combination license (funded by legislative appropriation).
programs.notes: Applied for via Go Outdoors Kansas annually; allow ~2 weeks processing.

programs.name: Kansas State Veterans Homes (Fort Dodge & Winfield)
programs.agency: Kansas Office of Veterans Services (KOVS)
programs.eligibility: Veterans who served on active duty with a discharge other than dishonorable. Preference for honorably-discharged wartime veterans; peacetime veterans, spouses, surviving spouses, and Gold Star parents on a space-available basis. Kansas residency not required but Kansas residents receive admission preference.
programs.coverage: Two homes: Kansas Soldiers' Home (Fort Dodge) and Kansas Veterans' Home (Winfield). Charges are based on ability to pay; no veteran is denied for lack of income.
programs.notes: The agency rebranded from the Kansas Commission on Veterans Affairs (kcva) to the Kansas Office of Veterans Services (kovs.ks.gov).

programs.name: State Income Tax on Military Retired Pay (Exempt)
programs.agency: Kansas Department of Revenue
programs.eligibility: Any recipient of U.S. Armed Forces retirement benefits, regardless of disability status. The benefit must be included in federal AGI before being subtracted on the Kansas return.
programs.coverage: 100% of military retirement pay is exempt from Kansas income tax (subtracted on Kansas Schedule S, Part A), including TSP distributions attributable to military service.
programs.notes: Kansas fully exempts military retired pay.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran Homestead Property Tax Credit
programs.agency: Iowa Department of Revenue (administered via county assessor)
programs.eligibility: Iowa resident who owns and occupies the homestead and is a veteran who acquired the homestead under specified federal programs (e.g., VA Specially Adapted Housing grant), OR has a permanent 100% service-connected disability rating (or permanent and total individual unemployability paid at the 100% rate). Surviving spouses/children receiving DIC may also qualify.
programs.coverage: 100% of the actual property tax levied on the homestead.
programs.notes: Separate from the general Military Service Property Tax Exemption; apply to the assessor by July 1 with a DD-214 and a current VA benefits letter.

programs.name: Military Service Property Tax Exemption
programs.agency: Iowa Department of Revenue (administered via county assessor)
programs.eligibility: Iowa resident honorably discharged veterans who served on active duty (generally 18 months, or qualifying wartime/Guard/Reserve service). Apply to the assessor by July 1.
programs.coverage: Reduction of taxable value: $4,000 for assessment years beginning on or after Jan 1, 2026 (raised from $1,852). This is a reduction in taxable value, not a dollar-for-dollar tax cut.
programs.notes: Distinct from the Disabled Veteran Homestead Credit; both can apply to the same property.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran License Plate & Registration Fee Exemption
programs.agency: Iowa Department of Transportation (Motor Vehicle Division), via county treasurer
programs.eligibility: A seriously disabled veteran who received federal financial assistance to purchase a vehicle under Title 38 U.S.C. §§ 3901–3904 (tied to the specific assisted vehicle). Separately, veterans rated 100% service-connected may be exempt from registration fees on up to three vehicles.
programs.coverage: DV plate issued at no cost, and the annual vehicle registration fee is waived for the qualifying vehicle. The 100%-rating exemption covers up to three vehicles (one free set of standard plates each).
programs.notes: Submit a DD-214 and IDVA documentation to the county treasurer. Confirm the 3-vehicle exemption detail with the county treasurer.

programs.name: Resident Disabled Veteran Lifetime Hunting & Fishing License
programs.agency: Iowa Department of Natural Resources (DNR)
programs.eligibility: Iowa resident (resident at least 90 days prior to applying) with a service-connected disability rating under Title 38, or a former POW. Requires a VA letter confirming the rating (and a Hunter Safety Certificate if applicable).
programs.coverage: $7.00 one-time total cost for the combined lifetime hunting AND fishing license.
programs.notes: A nominal flat lifetime fee, not strictly free.

programs.name: Iowa Veterans Home (Marshalltown)
programs.agency: Iowa Department of Veterans Affairs (IDVA)
programs.eligibility: Honorably discharged veterans, plus dependent/surviving spouses of honorably discharged veterans and Gold Star parents. Must meet Iowa residency on the date of admission and need residential or nursing care. Referrals through the county Veterans Service Office.
programs.coverage: State-operated residential and nursing/long-term care; resident cost share based on income/ability to pay.
programs.notes: Located in Marshalltown. Admissions: 800-645-4591.

programs.name: State Income Tax on Military Retired Pay (Exempt)
programs.agency: Iowa Department of Revenue
programs.eligibility: Any recipient of military retirement benefits, regardless of age; residents and nonresidents. Also applies to military survivor benefits under 10 U.S.C. 1447.
programs.coverage: 100% exclusion from Iowa individual income tax (full exemption of military retirement pay).
programs.notes: Enacted via Senate File 303 (2014), retroactive to tax years beginning on or after Jan 1, 2014. In addition to the general pension exclusion.

programs.name: Utah Veteran with a Disability Property Tax Exemption
programs.agency: Utah State Tax Commission (administered by county; certification via Utah Dept. of Veterans and Military Affairs)
programs.eligibility: Veterans with a service-connected disability of at least 10% (line-of-duty), their unmarried surviving spouse, or minor orphans. Must be a Utah resident; primary residence with up to 1 acre.
programs.coverage: Up to $535,459 of taxable value exempted (2026 maximum, CPI-adjusted annually). Benefit = maximum × disability percentage (e.g., a 50% rating exempts ~$267,730). No exemption below 10% disability.
programs.notes: Can apply to a primary residence and/or tangible personal property such as motor vehicles. Filing deadline Sept 1. Per Tax Commission Pub 36.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran (DV) License Plate
programs.agency: Utah Division of Motor Vehicles (DMV)
programs.eligibility: Veterans with a certified disabled status, documented by a letter from the Utah Department of Veterans and Military Affairs or another U.S. military entity.
programs.coverage: Standard plate fee $12.50 plus a $4.00 registration certificate fee; no special-plate contribution. The official DMV page does not state that registration or uniform fees are waived for the DV plate.
programs.notes: Vehicle fee relief in Utah is generally achieved via the Disabled Veteran Property Tax Exemption applied to the vehicle (tangible personal property), not via the plate itself. The DV plate does not confer handicapped parking.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran Hunting, Fishing, or Combination License (Discount)
programs.agency: Utah Division of Wildlife Resources (DWR)
programs.eligibility: Utah residents with a service-connected disability rating of 20% or greater, with VA or armed-forces verification.
programs.coverage: Discounted (not free): hunting license $25.50 (vs $34 standard); combination license $28.50 (vs $38); fishing license $12. One-time application; renews automatically at the discounted rate.
programs.notes: A reduced-rate program, not a free-license program.

programs.name: Utah State Veterans Homes (Nursing Homes)
programs.agency: Utah Department of Veterans and Military Affairs
programs.eligibility: Utah residents who served on active duty (or deployed while serving in the reserves), or have a service-connected injury/disability. Spouses of veterans and Gold Star Parents may also apply (their care is not VA-subsidized).
programs.coverage: No cost to veterans with a 70%+ service-connected disability. For veterans with lower/no service-connected disability, the VA provides a per-diem subsidy (about $120/day) toward the cost of care.
programs.notes: Four homes: William E. Christoffersen (Salt Lake City), George E. Wahlen (Ogden), Central Utah (Payson), and Southern Utah (Ivins).

programs.name: Military Retirement Income Tax Credit
programs.agency: Utah State Tax Commission
programs.eligibility: Taxpayer (or spouse, if filing jointly) who received taxable military retirement pay, including a survivor of a deceased service member. Military retirement income must be included in adjusted gross income.
programs.coverage: A nonrefundable credit equal to 4.5% of military retirement pay (multiply taxable military retirement pay by 0.045). Because Utah's income tax rate is effectively the same, the credit largely offsets state tax on military retirement income.
programs.notes: In place since the 2021 tax year. Cannot be claimed together with the general Retirement Credit. No carryforward of unused credit.

programs.name: Veterans' Property Tax Exemption (Base + Disabled-Veteran Additions)
programs.agency: Connecticut municipalities under CT OPM (CGS §§ 12-81, 12-81f, 12-81g)
programs.eligibility: Honorably discharged wartime veterans with 90+ days active service (or survivors). Additional disabled-veteran amounts require a VA service-connected disability rating. Income-tested additional exemptions available to qualifying veterans who meet state income limits. Towns may adopt higher local-option amounts.
programs.coverage: Base wartime-veteran exemption: $1,000 of assessed value (statutory minimum). Disabled veterans: an additional exemption scaled by VA rating, with enhanced minimums for severe disabilities. Beginning the 2024 assessment year, veterans rated 100% permanent and total receive a FULL exemption on one primary dwelling or motor vehicle.
programs.notes: Administered locally by each town assessor; exact dollar amounts vary by municipality, rating, and any local-option increase. Confirm specifics with the local assessor.

programs.name: Veteran and Disabled Veteran License Plates
programs.agency: Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) / CT Dept. of Veterans Affairs
programs.eligibility: Veteran plate: honorably discharged (or released under honorable conditions) from active service. Campaign-specific plates require proof of service via the appropriate Campaign Medal. Disabled American Veterans (DAV) plate: must be a DAV member with a vehicle registered in Connecticut.
programs.coverage: A fee is associated with the Veteran Plate Program; the exact dollar amount is not published on the official pages. Plate options include standard Veteran, Flag-Style Veteran, and wartime/campaign plates.
programs.notes: Apply via DMV Form M-46. Vehicle registration must not expire within 45 days of the request.

programs.name: Free Hunting/Fishing/Trapping License for Disabled Residents
programs.agency: Connecticut Department of Energy & Environmental Protection (DEEP)
programs.eligibility: Connecticut resident who has lost, or permanently lost the use of, one or more limbs may receive a free hunting/trapping license; a free recreational fishing license is available to residents who are permanently disabled (physician certification required). CT statute frames this around qualifying disability rather than a veteran-specific category.
programs.coverage: License issued free of charge (does not include required stamps/permits, which are still charged).
programs.notes: CT has no veteran-specific free-license code; many service-connected disabled veterans qualify under the general limb-loss/permanent-disability provisions. Confirm individual eligibility with DEEP.

programs.name: Connecticut State Veterans Home (Rocky Hill)
programs.agency: Connecticut Department of Veterans Affairs (DVA)
programs.eligibility: Honorably discharged or released under honorable conditions from active service, AND a current Connecticut resident or a Connecticut resident at the time of enlistment/induction. The residential facility requires 90+ days of active duty (other than training); the Healthcare Center additionally requires a chronic medical condition needing skilled nursing.
programs.coverage: State-operated domiciliary (residential) and skilled-nursing/healthcare facility. Resident cost-share is not a fixed published amount.
programs.notes: Located in Rocky Hill. Admission can be initiated by the veteran, a service officer, or a social-service agency.

programs.name: State Income Tax on Military Retired Pay (Exempt)
programs.agency: Connecticut Department of Revenue Services (DRS)
programs.eligibility: Retired members of the U.S. armed forces or National Guard, and beneficiaries receiving survivor benefits under an election made by a deceased retired military member.
programs.coverage: 100% of military retirement pay is exempt from Connecticut income tax (full subtraction modification), regardless of AGI.
programs.notes: Claimed as a subtraction modification on the CT return; military retirement pay is excluded from the pension/annuity income calculation.

programs.name: Veteran & Disabled Veteran Property Tax Exemption
programs.agency: NM Department of Veterans' Services / County Assessors (NM Taxation & Revenue)
programs.eligibility: Honorably discharged veteran who is a NM resident (base exemption). Disabled veteran exemption: veteran with a VA service-connected disability rating (10%–100%) occupying the property as principal residence; surviving spouses may retain it.
programs.coverage: Base exemption: $10,000 of taxable value (raised from $4,000 by HB47/2025, effective tax year 2025, inflation-indexed thereafter). Disabled veteran exemption: a property tax reduction proportional to the VA disability rating (e.g., a 70% rating = 70% reduction; 100% = full waiver), effective tax year 2026.
programs.notes: Implemented by 2024 Constitutional Amendments 1 and 2 via HB47 (signed March 2025). Previously only 100%-rated veterans received a full exemption.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran (DV) & Military Service License Plates
programs.agency: NM Motor Vehicle Division (MVD), Taxation & Revenue Dept.
programs.eligibility: 50% or greater service-connected disability rating (DV plate). Other veteran specialty plates available to qualifying veterans.
programs.coverage: Up to two free DV plates per qualifying veteran with no fees, including the regular registration fee waived. May instead choose up to two specialty plates with the registration fee waived (paying only the special-plate fee). Plates are permanent (no annual sticker).
programs.notes: Apply by mail using Form MVD10353 with a DD-214 and proof of disability.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran Hunting & Fishing License
programs.agency: NM Department of Game and Fish (NMDGF) / NM Dept. of Veterans' Services
programs.eligibility: NM resident veterans. The free lifetime card requires a 100% service-connected VA disability rating; a reduced rate applies for resident disabled veterans below 100%. Resident active-duty/honorably discharged veterans also get 50% off most licenses.
programs.coverage: 100% disabled: FREE lifetime Disabled Veteran Game-Hunting & Fishing license. Below 100% disabled: a $10 combination Game-Hunting & Fishing license. General military/veteran resident: 50% off most licenses, permits, and stamps.
programs.notes: 100%-disabled applicants submit the NMDGF Lifetime Resident Disabled Veteran Card Application with a DD-214 and VA Benefit Summary Letter. The 50% discount excludes federal duck stamps.

programs.name: New Mexico State Veterans' Home
programs.agency: NM Department of Health (operates the facility); NM Dept. of Veterans' Services (benefits)
programs.eligibility: Any honorably discharged U.S. Armed Forces veteran who was a NM resident at time of entering/discharge from service OR is a NM resident at date of admission. Gold Star Parents also eligible. Subject to bed availability.
programs.coverage: Long-term skilled nursing / domiciliary care. Costs offset by VA per diem and resident contribution. Located in Truth or Consequences, NM.

programs.name: State Income Tax on Military Retired Pay (Partial Exemption)
programs.agency: NM Taxation & Revenue Department
programs.eligibility: Armed forces retirees and their surviving spouses filing NM personal income tax (NMSA 1978, Sec. 7-2-5.13).
programs.coverage: Up to $30,000 of armed forces retirement pay exempt from NM personal income for tax year 2026 (and ongoing). Phase-in was $10,000 (2022), $20,000 (2023), $30,000 (2024 onward). Active-duty pay of NM-resident service members is separately 100% exempt.
programs.notes: The $30,000 exemption was made permanent by a 2024 amendment (effective Jan 1, 2025) that removed the prior sunset and extended eligibility to surviving spouses.

programs.name: Homestead Exemption for 100% Service-Connected Disabled Veterans
programs.agency: Nebraska Department of Revenue (Property Assessment Division) / Nebraska Dept. of Veterans' Affairs
programs.eligibility: Nebraska resident veteran with an honorable or general discharge who draws VA compensation for a 100% service-connected permanent disability OR holds a 100% Individual Unemployability rating; must own and occupy the homestead from Jan 1 through Aug 15, with the rating effective on or before Jan 1. Certain surviving spouses also qualify.
programs.coverage: 100% exemption of the homestead's taxable value. No income limitation and no homestead value maximum for this category.
programs.notes: File Form 458 plus VA certification. This category is filed once and re-certified only in years ending in 0 or 5.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran Plate & Motor Vehicle Tax/Fee Exemption
programs.agency: Nebraska Department of Motor Vehicles / Nebraska Dept. of Veterans' Affairs
programs.eligibility: DV License Plate: Nebraska veteran with honorable or general discharge and at least a 10% service-connected disability rating; must be enrolled in the NDVA Registry. Motor Vehicle Tax/Fee Exemption (effective Jan 1, 2026): disabled and/or blind veterans receiving VA compensation, also requiring Registry enrollment.
programs.coverage: DV plate: alphanumeric plate issued at no plate fee (a message/specialty DV plate is $40/year). Tax exemption: full exemption of the Motor Vehicle Tax and Motor Vehicle Fee on one personal-use vehicle (other charges still apply).
programs.notes: DV plate approval and the tax exemption are separate processes. The exemption covers only one vehicle and does not auto-transfer.

programs.name: Free Hunt/Fish/Fur-Harvest Permit & Lifetime Park Entry Permit
programs.agency: Nebraska Game and Parks Commission
programs.eligibility: Legal Nebraska resident rated by the VA as 50% or more disabled as a result of service, OR receiving a VA pension for total and permanent non-service-connected disability; honorable or general discharge.
programs.coverage: $0 — a combination fishing, fur-harvesting, and hunting permit plus habitat stamp, aquatic habitat stamp, and migratory waterfowl stamp; plus one perpetual Disabled Veterans' Lifetime Annual Park Entry Permit at no fee.
programs.notes: The free combination permit is perpetual and voids only if the veteran loses eligibility. (Non-disabled resident veterans 64+ qualify for a $5 Veteran's Annual Small Game permit.)

programs.name: Nebraska Veterans' Homes (Bellevue, Kearney, Norfolk, Scottsbluff)
programs.agency: Nebraska Department of Veterans' Affairs
programs.eligibility: Veterans who served on active duty with an honorable or general discharge and lived in Nebraska at least two years during their lifetime, and who are disabled by reason of service, age, or otherwise unable to earn a living. Spouses, surviving spouses, and Gold Star spouses/parents may also qualify.
programs.coverage: Members are admitted regardless of financial situation; those able to pay contribute a portion based on income and assets. Services: domiciliary, assisted living, skilled nursing, and memory care.
programs.notes: Four state homes: Eastern (Bellevue), Central (Kearney), Norfolk, and Western (Scottsbluff). Apply via the County Veterans' Service Officer.

programs.name: State Income Tax on Military Retired Pay (Exempt)
programs.agency: Nebraska Department of Revenue
programs.eligibility: Any military retiree receiving qualifying military retirement benefits (including Coast Guard, USPHS Commissioned Corps, and NOAA Commissioned Officer Corps), to the extent included in federal AGI.
programs.coverage: 100% of military retirement benefits excluded from Nebraska taxable income, for tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2022.
programs.notes: No election or form is required (the former one-time election was eliminated). Enacted by LB387.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran Real Property Tax Credit
programs.agency: West Virginia Tax Division (with WV Dept. of Veterans Assistance certification)
programs.eligibility: Honorably discharged veterans with a 90% or greater combined service-connected disability rating (or eligible widowed spouse) who own and have occupied their WV homestead for at least 6 months. Property taxes must be paid on time.
programs.coverage: A refundable income tax credit equal to 100% of the WV ad valorem real property taxes timely paid on the homestead for the year. If the credit exceeds income tax liability, the excess is refunded.
programs.notes: Enacted under WV Code Art. 11-13MM; claimed by filing Form DV-1 with the IT-140. A separate general $20,000 assessed-value homestead exemption also exists for residents 65+ or permanently/totally disabled.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran License Plate (DV plate)
programs.agency: WV Division of Motor Vehicles (DMV)
programs.eligibility: 100% total and permanent service-connected disability rating, or recipient of a federal Specially Adapted Vehicle grant. Part 2 of the application must be certified by the WV Dept. of Veterans Assistance. Free plates also available to former POWs, Purple Heart recipients, and Pearl Harbor survivors.
programs.coverage: No registration fee for one DV plate; applicant pays only the $0.50 insurance enforcement fee and $1.00 litter fee per remaining year of the 10-year cycle. Other (non-disabled) veteran plates cost a one-time $10 over the regular fee.
programs.notes: Apply with DMV-48-D / DMV-48-DI.

programs.name: Free Hunting & Fishing License (Disabled Veterans / Former POWs)
programs.agency: WV Division of Natural Resources (WVDNR)
programs.eligibility: WV resident, honorably discharged, who receives VA compensation/pension for a 100% total and permanent service-connected disability; was a prisoner of war; or is eligible for the motor-vehicle registration fee exemption. Authority: WV Code 20-2-28.
programs.coverage: Free — may hunt, trap, and fish in WV without purchasing a license.
programs.notes: WVDNR License Unit: (304) 558-2758.

programs.name: State Veterans Home (Barboursville) & Veterans Nursing Facility (Clarksburg)
programs.agency: WV Dept. of Veterans Assistance
programs.eligibility: Barboursville (domiciliary): honorable/general discharge; ambulatory and independent in activities of daily living; eligible for VA Medical Center care; minimum active-duty service requirement. Clarksburg (skilled nursing): WV resident for 12 consecutive months and served on active duty.
programs.coverage: Income is not a factor for admission; residents contribute one-half of their monthly income as a maintenance contribution. The nursing facility provides skilled nursing care (varies by care/VA per-diem).
programs.notes: Two distinct facilities. Pre-admission medical tests required.

programs.name: State Income Tax on Military Retired Pay (Exempt)
programs.agency: West Virginia Tax Division
programs.eligibility: All military retirees — regular Armed Forces, Reserves, National Guard, U.S. Public Health Service Commissioned Corps, and NOAA Commissioned Officer Corps; survivorship annuitants also qualify.
programs.coverage: 100% exempt — West Virginia does not tax any military retired pay (effective tax years on or after Jan 1, 2019).
programs.notes: Claimed as a decreasing modification on Schedule M of Form IT-140.

programs.name: Property Tax Benefit for Veterans with a 100% Service-Connected Disability
programs.agency: Idaho State Tax Commission
programs.eligibility: Veteran recognized by the VA as having a 100% service-connected disability, or receiving 100% compensation due to individual unemployability, as of January 1. Must own and occupy an Idaho home as primary residence and have a current homeowner's exemption. No income limit.
programs.coverage: Reduces property tax by up to $1,500 on the home and up to one acre of land.
programs.notes: Only a 100% rating (or 100% IU) qualifies. Apply Jan 1 – Apr 15; auto-renews if the disability is permanent and total. Separate from the income-based Property Tax Reduction (circuit breaker).

programs.name: Disabled Veteran License Plates (Registration Fee Exemption)
programs.agency: Idaho Transportation Department — Division of Motor Vehicles
programs.eligibility: Veteran receiving VA compensation for a 100% service-connected disability, OR with loss/permanent loss of use of one or both feet or hands, or virtual blindness in both eyes. Requires an ITD Eligibility Letter (via the VA Regional Office Boise) plus Form ITD 3397.
programs.coverage: $0 registration/reregistration fee on one vehicle; a DV plate is issued.
programs.notes: Per Idaho Code 49-403. The fee exemption applies to one motor vehicle.

programs.name: Disabled American Veteran (DAV) Reduced-Fee Hunting & Fishing License
programs.agency: Idaho Department of Fish and Game
programs.eligibility: Idaho resident veteran with a VA-verified service-connected disability rating of 40% or greater (submit VA letter). A nonresident DAV program is also available.
programs.coverage: Resident DAV combination license $5; reduced-fee DAV tags (deer $10.75, elk $16.50, bear $6.75, turkey $10.75). Resident veterans rated 100% service-connected also get free State Park campsite and day-use access.
programs.notes: A separate Disabled Veterans Special Big Game Tag Program lets a qualified organization obtain a free special hunt tag on behalf of a disabled veteran.

programs.name: Idaho State Veterans Homes
programs.agency: Idaho Division of Veterans Services
programs.eligibility: Veterans who can no longer provide for themselves and need long-term care; admission via the Idaho State Veterans Home Application for Admission.
programs.coverage: Long-term skilled nursing / supportive care at four facilities: Boise, Lewiston, Pocatello, and Post Falls. Cost-share based on VA per diem, veteran income, and applicable rates.
programs.notes: Contact the Central Support Office (208) 780-1300 for the admission application and detailed criteria.

programs.name: State Income Tax on Military Retired Pay (Retirement Benefits Deduction)
programs.agency: Idaho State Tax Commission
programs.eligibility: Recipient of qualifying military retired pay who is at least age 65, OR at least age 62 and classified as disabled. The maximum is reduced dollar-for-dollar by Social Security and Railroad Retirement benefits received.
programs.coverage: Tax year 2025 maximum deduction: $48,216 single / $72,324 married filing jointly, less any Social Security and Railroad Retirement benefits received. The state recalculates the maximum each year.
programs.notes: Idaho has no separate blanket military-retirement exemption beyond this age/disability-gated deduction. The TY2026 amounts were not yet published as of mid-2026.

programs.name: Real Property Tax Exemption for Totally Disabled Veterans
programs.agency: Hawaii county real property tax offices (Honolulu, Hawaii, Maui, Kauai) — referred by the State Office of Veterans' Services
programs.eligibility: Veteran totally disabled (100%) due to injuries sustained on active duty, owning and occupying the property as a home; honorable discharge and VA certification required. An unremarried widow(er) who continues to own and occupy the home also qualifies. Administered at the county level.
programs.coverage: Exempts the home from all real property taxes except the county minimum tax (e.g., Honolulu's annual minimum). Each county sets its own minimum-tax amount.
programs.notes: Property tax is county-administered in Hawaii (no statewide rate). Honolulu uses Form E-8-10.5. Confirm the exact minimum-tax figure with your county office.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran License Plates & Registration Fee Exemption
programs.agency: Hawaii Office of Veterans' Services / county motor vehicle registration offices
programs.eligibility: Hawaii resident, honorable discharge, and a 100% service-connected disability rating from the VA. Veteran/specialty plates are available to qualifying veterans more broadly.
programs.coverage: A $46.00 state registration fee exemption on one vehicle for 100% service-connected disabled veterans. Specialty/veteran license plates are issued for the same cost as a regular plate.
programs.notes: County weight tax is separate; some islands offer a county-level vehicle/weight-tax exemption for totally disabled veterans — confirm with the county.

programs.name: Hunting & Fishing License (No Veteran-Specific Discount)
programs.agency: Hawaii Dept. of Land and Natural Resources (DLNR)
programs.eligibility: General resident licensing. DLNR runs a Disabled Public Hunting program offering accommodations for disabled hunters, but eligibility is not veteran-specific.
programs.coverage: Resident hunting license $10.00. Hawaii has no veteran-specific free or reduced hunting license, and the state issues no resident marine recreational fishing license at all.
programs.notes: Unlike most states, Hawaii does not offer a disabled-veteran hunting/fishing discount. The Disabled Public Hunting program serves disabled hunters generally, not veterans specifically.

programs.name: Yukio Okutsu State Veterans Home (Hilo)
programs.agency: Hawaii Office of Veterans' Services; operated via Hilo Medical Center
programs.eligibility: Requires skilled or long-term nursing care; at least 55 years old (younger cases reviewed individually); honorably discharged; a Hawaii resident either before entering the Armed Forces or for at least one year prior to applying; able to cover the resident's share of care costs. Spouses, surviving spouses, and Gold Star parents may be admitted as space allows.
programs.coverage: A 95-bed skilled nursing / long-term care facility in Hilo. Cost is shared; VA per-diem and the resident's share apply.
programs.notes: Contact (808) 961-1500 for availability.

programs.name: State Income Tax on Military Retired Pay (Exempt)
programs.agency: Hawaii Department of Taxation
programs.eligibility: Recipients of military retired pay (all branches). SBP, RCSBP, and RSFPP survivor annuities are likewise exempt.
programs.coverage: 100% exempt from Hawaii state income tax (military retired pay remains taxable at the federal level).
programs.notes: Hawaii fully exempts military retirement pay under the public-pension exclusion (HRS §235-7). National Guard/Reserve drill pay also has a partial exemption.

programs.name: Veterans' Property Tax Credits & Adapted-Homestead Exemption
programs.agency: New Hampshire municipalities (local assessors) under state statute; NH Division of Veterans Services for guidance
programs.eligibility: Honorably discharged/separated veterans who own NH residential property. The standard/All Veterans' credit applies to qualifying veterans (the All Veterans' credit requires the town to have adopted it). The service-connected total disability credit (RSA 72:35) applies to veterans with a permanent and total service-connected disability. The adapted-homestead exemption (RSA 72:36-a) applies to a 100% permanently and totally disabled veteran whose home was acquired/adapted with a VA SAH/SHA grant.
programs.coverage: Standard veterans' tax credit: $50 (town may adopt $51 up to $750). All Veterans' tax credit: same amount as the town's standard/optional credit. Service-connected total disability credit: $700 (town may adopt $701 up to $5,000). Adapted-homestead: FULL exemption of the homestead from property tax.
programs.notes: Amounts are set by each city/town within these state ranges, so the actual credit varies by municipality; figures shown are the statutory minimums/maximums.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran (DV) License Plate
programs.agency: NH Department of Safety, Division of Motor Vehicles (DMV)
programs.eligibility: Honorably discharged veteran who is rated totally and permanently disabled from a service-connected disability, totally blind from a service-connected cause, or a service-connected amputee/paraplegic who received federal funds for a specially adapted vehicle. One plate per eligible veteran (RSA 261:86).
programs.coverage: $0 — plate issued at no charge; vehicles displaying the DV plate with the international accessibility symbol park free in any NH city or town when under the owner's direct control.
programs.notes: Statutory basis RSA 261:86 (plate) and RSA 265:73 (free parking).

programs.name: Disabled Veteran's Hunting and Fishing License
programs.agency: New Hampshire Fish and Game Department
programs.eligibility: NH resident, discharge other than dishonorable. Full benefit: totally and permanently disabled from a service-connected disability. Reduced benefit: at least 80% but less than 100% permanently service-connected disabled for more than 2 years.
programs.coverage: 100% permanently/totally service-connected disabled: a perpetual (lifetime) combination hunting/fishing license for a one-time $10 administrative fee. 80–99% (2+ years): a lifetime license at 50% of the standard lifetime cost.
programs.notes: Authority RSA 214:13. The 100% license is effectively free aside from the single $10 admin fee.

programs.name: New Hampshire Veterans Home (Tilton)
programs.agency: New Hampshire Veterans Home
programs.eligibility: Honorably discharged veteran who is medically qualified for the level of care provided; must have been a NH resident for at least one year prior to application OR have had NH as 'home of record' on discharge papers. Financial certification required (one-year asset look-back).
programs.coverage: A state veterans long-term care/skilled nursing home; resident contribution toward room and board is based on assets and income (means-tested). A residence is not counted as an asset while occupied by a spouse, partner, or dependent.
programs.notes: Located in Tilton; Admissions (603) 527-4400.

programs.name: State Income Tax on Military Retired Pay (None)
programs.agency: New Hampshire Department of Revenue Administration
programs.eligibility: All New Hampshire residents, including military retirees.
programs.coverage: New Hampshire imposes no state tax on earned income or on pensions/retirement income, including military retired pay.
programs.notes: NH never taxed earned income or pensions; its only personal income-type tax (the Interest & Dividends tax) was fully repealed effective for tax periods beginning on or after Jan 1, 2025. As of 2025 NH has no individual income tax of any kind.

programs.name: Veteran Property Tax Exemption
programs.agency: Maine Revenue Services / Municipal Assessors
programs.eligibility: Maine resident veteran with a discharge other than dishonorable who served during a recognized war period AND is age 62+, OR is receiving 100% VA disability, OR became 100% disabled while serving. Also extends to surviving spouses, minor children, and surviving parents. A separate paraplegic exemption applies to veterans who received a federal specially adapted housing grant.
programs.coverage: $6,000 deducted from the just (assessed) value of the estate for qualifying wartime veterans; $50,000 deducted for paraplegic veterans (or those who received a federal specially adapted housing grant).
programs.notes: Applied through the local municipal tax assessor; written notice with proof of eligibility required only with the first application.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran License Plate & Vehicle Fee Exemption
programs.agency: Maine Secretary of State, Bureau of Motor Vehicles (BMV)
programs.eligibility: Veteran with a 100% service-connected disability that is permanent and total and receiving 100% benefits, OR a veteran with loss of/loss of use of both legs. Vehicle registered gross weight cannot exceed 26,000 lbs.
programs.coverage: Disabled Veteran plate: exempt from excise tax, registration fee, and title fee. Other no-fee veteran plates (Purple Heart, Medal of Honor, Former POW, Pearl Harbor Survivor, Gold Star Family) are registration-fee exempt up to 10,000 lbs.
programs.notes: Requires a DD-214 and VA rating letter.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran Complimentary Hunting & Fishing License
programs.agency: Maine Dept. of Inland Fisheries & Wildlife / Bureau of Maine Veterans' Services
programs.eligibility: Veteran with a service-connected disability rated at 50% or more who meets Maine residency requirements (also available to residents of certain reciprocal states).
programs.coverage: A free (complimentary) lifetime combination license covering fishing, trapping, hunting, archery, muzzleloader, bear, migratory bird, pheasant, turkey, coyote night hunt, and crossbow.
programs.notes: Valid for the life of the holder while residency is maintained. Any-deer and moose permits must still be applied for each year. Obtained via the Bureau of Maine Veterans' Services (Augusta).

programs.name: Maine Veterans' Homes
programs.agency: Maine Veterans' Homes (state-chartered) / Bureau of Maine Veterans' Services
programs.eligibility: Honorably discharged veteran who served one or more days of active duty and was a Maine resident at time of entry into service OR is a Maine resident at time of application. Spouses, widows/widowers, and Gold Star parents may also be eligible (spouses must qualify for nursing-home or assisted-living level of care).
programs.coverage: Six facilities: Augusta, Bangor, Caribou, Machias, Scarborough, and South Paris. Long-term/nursing care, assisted living, rehabilitation, and therapy. Cost via private pay, VA per-diem, or MaineCare.
programs.notes: No combat service or service-connected disability required.

programs.name: State Income Tax on Military Retired Pay (Exempt)
programs.agency: Maine Revenue Services
programs.eligibility: Any Maine taxpayer receiving benefits under a military retirement plan (active or reserve), including survivor benefit payments.
programs.coverage: 100% exempt from Maine state income tax. For tax years beginning on or after Jan 1, 2016, military retirement benefits (including survivor benefits) are fully exempt. Unlike the general pension deduction, the military exemption is not reduced by Social Security and is not capped.
programs.notes: Claimed as a subtraction on Form 1040ME Schedule 1S. SBP annuities are also not taxed.

programs.name: Montana Disabled Veteran (MDV) Property Tax Assistance Program
programs.agency: Montana Department of Revenue
programs.eligibility: Veteran rated 100% service-connected disabled (or paid at the 100% rate), who owns and occupies the home as a primary residence at least 7 months/year; or an unmarried surviving spouse. Must meet income limits and apply by April 15.
programs.coverage: A property tax rate reduction of 100%, 80%, 70%, or 50% based on income (Tax Year 2026). Single: 100% up to $48,152, scaling down to 50% at $57,782–$62,598. Married/Head of Household and surviving-spouse brackets differ. Applies to the home and up to 1 acre.
programs.notes: The reduction applies to the property tax rate, not a flat dollar amount. Income brackets are inflation-adjusted each year.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran (DV) License Plate & Registration Fee Waiver
programs.agency: Montana Motor Vehicle Division (Dept. of Justice); administered at county treasurer offices
programs.eligibility: Per MCA 61-3-460: a complete fee waiver for veterans rated 100% disabled (or paid at the 100% rate), former POWs, and unmarried surviving spouses of service members killed on active duty. Purple Heart recipients rated 50%+ get the registration fee waived but still owe the cemetery fee. Applies to up to two non-commercial vehicles.
programs.coverage: 100% waiver of motor vehicle registration fees (and the veterans' cemetery fee for the fully-exempt categories) on up to two non-commercial vehicles.
programs.notes: Apply at the local county treasurer with a VA disability letter and DD-214. Statutory basis MCA 61-3-460.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran & Military Hunting/Fishing Licenses
programs.agency: Montana Fish, Wildlife & Parks (FWP)
programs.eligibility: Resident veterans with certain combat-connected injuries qualify for half-price deer and antelope licenses (via the FWP Combat Disabled Application). A separate donated-license program serves disabled veterans sponsored by a qualifying nonprofit. Resident Purple Heart recipients may fish and hunt upland game birds with a Conservation License.
programs.coverage: Half price (50% off) on deer and antelope licenses for combat-disabled resident veterans; up to 50 such licenses issued annually.
programs.notes: FWP Licensing 406-444-2950 for specifics on disability-percentage thresholds.

programs.name: State Veterans' Homes (Columbia Falls & Glendive)
programs.agency: Montana Department of Public Health and Human Services (DPHHS)
programs.eligibility: Honorably discharged veterans; spouses and unmarried surviving spouses (admitted on a space-available basis). The applicant must qualify medically for skilled/intermediate nursing or domiciliary care. Open-admission policy regardless of ability to pay.
programs.coverage: Montana Veterans' Home (Columbia Falls): 105 intermediate/skilled-care beds plus 12 domiciliary beds. Eastern Montana Veterans' Home (Glendive): 80 intermediate/skilled-care beds including a 16-bed Special Care Unit. Cost offset by VA per diem, Medicare/Medicaid, and resident contribution.
programs.notes: Verify the age requirement and current criteria with the Admission Coordinator (406-897-6091).

programs.name: State Income Tax on Military Retired Pay (Partial Exemption)
programs.agency: Montana Department of Revenue
programs.eligibility: Montana resident military retirees receiving retired pay from DFAS, and resident recipients of military survivor benefits. Must have become a MT resident after June 30, 2023, OR have been a resident before receiving the retirement income and remained one. Claimed on Form WMRE.
programs.coverage: Exempts 50% of military retirement income (and qualifying survivor benefits) received from DFAS from Montana taxable income.
programs.notes: Partial 50% exemption effective tax year 2024. SB 93 (2025) eliminated the prior sunset, effective for tax years after Dec 31, 2025. Confirm the current claim mechanics against DOR guidance.

programs.name: Veterans' Property Tax Exemption (incl. Disabled / Totally Disabled)
programs.agency: RI Office of Veterans Services / local city & town tax assessors
programs.eligibility: Honorably discharged veteran (and unmarried surviving spouse). Enhanced tiers for service-connected totally disabled veterans, recipients of VA specially-adapted-housing grants, and ex-POWs. Apply through your town tax assessor with a DD-214.
programs.coverage: State minimums (off assessed value): $1,000 base veteran exemption; $10,000 for service-connected totally disabled; an additional $10,000 for VA specially-adapted housing; $15,000 ex-POW. Cities/towns MAY increase any amount by local ordinance, so the actual benefit varies by municipality.
programs.notes: State law sets mandatory minimum exemptions; larger amounts are local-option. Gold Star parents are covered separately under RIGL 44-3-5.

programs.name: Veteran & Disabled Veteran License Plates + Fee Exemption
programs.agency: RI Division of Motor Vehicles (DMV)
programs.eligibility: Veteran, Disabled Veteran, Ex-POW, Purple Heart, and Gold Star Family plates available with documentation. The Disabled Veteran registration & license fee exemption requires an honorable wartime-period discharge AND one of: loss/loss-of-use of a limb; a VA specially-adapted-vehicle grant; a 100% combined service-connected rating; or VA individual unemployability.
programs.coverage: Qualifying wartime disabled veterans are exempt from RI vehicle registration fees and driver's license fees (per RIGL 31-6-8). A 100% service-connected Disabled Veteran license holder is exempt from license costs for life.
programs.notes: Plate types confirmed on dmv.ri.gov; fee-exemption criteria codified at RIGL 31-6-8.

programs.name: Free Hunting & Fishing License for 100% Disabled Veterans
programs.agency: RI Department of Environmental Management (DEM)
programs.eligibility: Rhode Island resident veteran with 100% (total) VA disability status. Must present a current original final-decision document from the VA.
programs.coverage: A no-cost (free) freshwater fishing, hunting, or combination license. 100%-disabled veterans are also exempt from needing a saltwater fishing license (must carry the original VA decision document while fishing).
programs.notes: Reissued annually after confirmation the status is still 100%. Statutory basis RIGL 20-2-31.

programs.name: Rhode Island Veterans Home (Bristol)
programs.agency: RI Office of Veterans Services
programs.eligibility: Honorably discharged veteran with at least 90 days of active wartime service, AND either inducted/enlisted to RI's quota OR a Rhode Island resident for 2 consecutive years immediately prior to application. All ages eligible if the wartime requirement is met. Voluntary admission subject to medical director approval.
programs.coverage: Residents contribute to their care based on financial means, typically set at 80% of adjusted net income.
programs.notes: Located in Bristol; (401) 253-8000.

programs.name: State Income Tax on Military Retired Pay (Exempt)
programs.agency: RI Division of Taxation
programs.eligibility: Any taxpayer receiving military service pension benefits included in federal AGI. No age limit and no income cap.
programs.coverage: 100% exemption — full subtraction of military service pension income from RI taxable income. Effective for tax years beginning on or after Jan 1, 2023. Service-connected disability retired pay is also exempt.
programs.notes: Codified at RIGL 44-30-12(c). Note: TSP distributions remain taxable by RI; only military service pension is exempted.

programs.name: Disabled Veterans Property Tax Credit
programs.agency: North Dakota Office of State Tax Commissioner
programs.eligibility: Veteran with an honorable discharge and a VA service-connected disability of 50% or greater (or an extra-schedular rating, including individual unemployability, paid at the 100% rate) who owns and resides on the homestead. Unremarried surviving spouse, or spouse receiving VA dependency and indemnity compensation, may also qualify.
programs.coverage: Reduction of taxable value scaled to the disability rating: 100% = $9,000, 90% = $8,100, down to 50% = $4,500 of the homestead's taxable value. Because the cap is on taxable value (a small fraction of market value), the effective market-value relief is substantially larger.
programs.notes: Apply to the local assessor or county director of tax equalization by April 1.

programs.name: Disabled American Veteran (DAV) License Plate
programs.agency: North Dakota Department of Transportation / ND Department of Veterans Affairs
programs.eligibility: Veteran certified by the VA as 100% service-connected disabled (or an extra-schedular/individual-unemployability rating totaling 100%). Unremarried surviving spouse may retain one DAV plate.
programs.coverage: No annual license (registration) fee, and exempt from state sales/use tax on the vehicle. Applies to up to two vehicles under 26,000 lbs.
programs.notes: DAV plate holders may park in designated handicap spots without an additional placard. Apply via Form SFN 2872 with a VA certification letter.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran Hunting & Fishing Licenses
programs.agency: North Dakota Game and Fish Department
programs.eligibility: Resident veterans. The reduced fishing license requires a 50% or greater service-connected disability; the reduced combined hunting license requires a 100% service-connected disability (or individual unemployability).
programs.coverage: Reduced fishing license: $10 plus a $2 certificate fee. Veteran combined hunting license: $10 plus a $2 certificate and $20 general game/habitat fees.
programs.notes: Reduced-rate, not free. Apply via ND Game and Fish online licensing.

programs.name: North Dakota Veterans Home (Lisbon)
programs.agency: North Dakota Veterans Home / ND Department of Veterans Affairs
programs.eligibility: Veterans who served on continuous federalized active duty (180 days or the full period ordered) discharged under other than dishonorable conditions; also spouses and surviving spouses of qualifying veterans. North Dakota residency preceding application (may be waived for those who served in a ND regiment).
programs.coverage: 111 basic-care beds and 38 skilled-nursing beds. Resident cost is based on care level and means.
programs.notes: Located in Lisbon. Tiered admission priorities favor service-connected disabled veterans, ex-POWs, and disabled National Guard members.

programs.name: State Income Tax on Military Retired Pay (Exempt)
programs.agency: North Dakota Office of State Tax Commissioner
