programs.eligibility: Retired members of the U.S. Armed Forces, Reserve, and National Guard, and their surviving spouses.
programs.coverage: 100% of the federally-taxable military retirement benefit is deductible from North Dakota taxable income, effectively exempting it from ND state income tax.
programs.notes: Enacted by HB 1053 (2019), effective tax year 2019 onward. Attach Form 1099-R from DFAS to claim.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran Property Tax Exemption (Dwelling)
programs.agency: South Dakota Department of Revenue / Department of Veterans Affairs (county Director of Equalization administers)
programs.eligibility: Veteran rated permanently and totally disabled from a service-connected disability who owns and occupies the dwelling (SDCL 10-4-40). Surviving spouses qualify for a separate, lower exemption. Application filed annually with the county Director of Equalization by November 1.
programs.coverage: $200,000 of the full and true value of the dwelling is exempt for the disabled veteran; $150,000 for qualifying surviving spouses.
programs.notes: Covers the house, attached garage, and lot up to one acre. The exemption was raised to $200,000 in 2024.

programs.name: Paraplegic Veteran Property Tax Exemption
programs.agency: South Dakota Department of Revenue / county Director of Equalization
programs.eligibility: Veterans with the loss, or loss of use, of both lower extremities, who own and occupy a dwelling specifically designed for use by paraplegics (SDCL 10-4-24.10). The veteran must occupy the property for one full calendar year before the exemption takes effect.
programs.coverage: 100% exemption from property taxation on the qualifying wheelchair-designed dwelling.
programs.notes: Distinct from the $200,000 dwelling exemption — this is a full exemption on a specially designed home.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran License Plate
programs.agency: South Dakota Department of Revenue, Motor Vehicle Division
programs.eligibility: Resident veteran who received a VA 'K' Award, an automobile under Public Law 187, a statutory benefit for loss/loss of use of one or more extremities, or a veteran's allotment for total disability from a service-connected injury incurred during wartime or armed conflict.
programs.coverage: $10 annual plate fee (no vehicle registration fee charged) plus a $7.50 mailing fee.
programs.notes: South Dakota also offers a free 'Veteran' designation on a driver's license or ID card at renewal.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran & POW Reduced-Fee Hunting and Fishing License
programs.agency: South Dakota Game, Fish & Parks (GFP)
programs.eligibility: South Dakota resident who receives a VA 'K' Award or a veteran's allotment for a 40% or greater service-connected disability; OR is 40%+ disabled for Social Security purposes with verified active military service; OR was a Prisoner of War.
programs.coverage: A $10 fee for a license valid for four years (replaces the resident Small Game license and resident Fishing license).
programs.notes: Reduced flat fee, not free. The GFP threshold (40%) differs from the property-tax 'permanent and total' standard.

programs.name: State Income Tax on Military Retired Pay (None)
programs.agency: South Dakota Department of Revenue
programs.eligibility: All South Dakota residents, including military retirees.
programs.coverage: South Dakota has NO state individual income tax, so military retired pay, active-duty pay, VA disability, pensions, and TSP distributions are all fully exempt from state income tax.
programs.notes: One of the states with no individual income tax.

programs.name: Disabled Veterans School Property Tax Credit
programs.agency: Delaware Department of Finance, Division of Revenue (with county/local tax offices)
programs.eligibility: Delaware resident with a 100% service-connected, permanent and total disability rating from the VA (including 100% based on individual unemployability). Must have held legal domicile in Delaware for the 3 years immediately preceding application; credit applies only to the primary residence; all prior property tax liabilities must be paid. Cannot be combined with the Senior School Property Tax Credit. Application due April 30.
programs.coverage: A credit against 100% of the non-vocational school district property tax on the primary residence.
programs.notes: Effective beginning tax year 2022. The credit is for the qualifying veteran (surviving spouse not covered).

programs.name: Disabled American Veteran (DAV) License Plate & Registration Fee Exemption
programs.agency: Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles (DMV)
programs.eligibility: Veterans with a VA-certified service-connected disability who are eligible for adaptive-equipment benefits (per 21 Del. C. § 2164). Requires a Delaware driver license/ID and VA documentation (Form MV549DAV). A surviving spouse may retain the plate.
programs.coverage: A $10 one-time administrative fee for the DAV plate; registration fees waived for one vehicle per eligible veteran at any one time.
programs.notes: Annual vehicle inspection still required.

programs.name: Disabled Veterans Hunting, Trapping & Fishing License Exemption
programs.agency: Delaware Department of Natural Resources and Environmental Control (DNREC)
programs.eligibility: Delaware residents honorably discharged and certified by the VA as having at least a 60% service-connected disability. Requires a written VA statement; apply via the Veterans with Disabilities Exempt Application.
programs.coverage: Free (no charge) — an exemption to hunt, trap, and fish statewide.
programs.notes: Per 7 Del. C. § 502. Contact 302-739-9918.

programs.name: Delaware Veterans Home (Milford)
programs.agency: State of Delaware — Delaware Veterans Home
programs.eligibility: Honorably discharged from active service (or qualifying National Guard/Reservist); must currently reside in Delaware for at least 1 year prior to application; and must meet federal and state requirements for skilled nursing home level of care. Spouses of veteran residents are also eligible, subject to space availability.
programs.coverage: A 144-bed skilled nursing facility in Milford. Costs are means-based with VA per-diem support.
programs.notes: Admissions: (302) 424-8572.

programs.name: State Income Tax on Military Retired Pay (Pension Exclusion)
programs.agency: Delaware Department of Finance, Division of Revenue
programs.eligibility: Delaware resident taxpayers receiving a U.S. military pension. Under 30 Del. C. § 1106, taxpayers under age 60 may exclude the greater of up to $2,000 (general pension) OR up to $12,500 as a U.S. military pension; taxpayers 60+ may exclude up to $12,500 of pensions/eligible retirement income.
programs.coverage: Up to $12,500 of military retired pay excluded from Delaware taxable income (current 2026 statutory amount).
programs.notes: A bill to phase the exclusion up to $25,000 by tax year 2029 (SB219) was pending and not yet in effect; the current figure is $12,500. Delaware has no broader military-retirement exemption.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran Property Tax Exemption
programs.agency: Alaska Dept. of Commerce, Community, and Economic Development (administered by municipalities); statutory basis AS 29.45.030(e)
programs.eligibility: Alaska-resident veteran owning and occupying the property as primary residence, with a service-connected disability rated 50% or more. A companion senior-citizen exemption applies to residents age 65+. The exemption may transfer to a surviving spouse who is at least 60.
programs.coverage: The first $150,000 of assessed value of the primary residence is exempt (mandatory statewide minimum under AS 29.45.030(e)). Municipalities may grant exemptions above $150,000.
programs.notes: All Alaska municipalities must grant the first $150,000 exemption. Application is filed locally with the municipal assessor.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran (DV) License Plates & Free Registration
programs.agency: Alaska Dept. of Administration, Division of Motor Vehicles (DMV)
programs.eligibility: Veterans with VA certification of a combined service-related disability of 50% or more qualify for Disabled Veteran (DV) plates. DV plates with parking privileges also require a Special Disability Parking Permit.
programs.coverage: One free vehicle registration for a person holding a disability parking permit/plate (registration fee waived on one vehicle). Standard fees apply to additional vehicles.
programs.notes: Alaska registers passenger vehicles on a 2-year cycle; the waiver covers one vehicle. A Veteran designation on a driver's license is also available with proof of honorable service.

programs.name: Resident Disabled Veteran Hunting / Fishing / Trapping License
programs.agency: Alaska Department of Fish and Game (ADF&G)
programs.eligibility: Must meet ADF&G's residency definition AND be certified 50% disabled or greater (service-connected). Must be physically present in Alaska to apply and provide a VA Benefit Summary Letter. The card is void if the holder ceases to be an Alaska resident.
programs.coverage: A free permanent identification card authorizing hunting, sport fishing, and trapping at no cost. Holders are also exempt from the king salmon stamp and the state duck/waterfowl conservation stamp.
programs.notes: Documentation may be submitted online or to ADF&G Licensing, Juneau.

programs.name: Alaska Veterans and Pioneers Home (Palmer)
programs.agency: Alaska Dept. of Family and Community Services, Division of Alaska Pioneer Homes
programs.eligibility: Honorably separated veterans age 65 or older who have resided in Alaska continuously for at least one year immediately preceding application and need assisted-living/long-term care. 75% of beds are reserved for eligible veterans.
programs.coverage: 79 total beds (about 75% designated for veterans). Monthly fees are based on the resident's ability to pay and assessed level of care; qualifying veterans receive a VA per diem.
programs.notes: No cost to join the waitlist. Contact 888-355-3117. Alaska's only combined state veterans/pioneers home.

programs.name: State Income Tax on Military Retired Pay (None)
programs.agency: Alaska Department of Revenue, Tax Division
programs.eligibility: All Alaska residents, including military retirees.
programs.coverage: Alaska has NO state personal income tax. Military retired pay and all other personal income is not taxed by the state, and no state income tax return is required.
programs.notes: Federal income tax still applies. Alaska also has no statewide sales tax (though some municipalities levy local sales taxes).

programs.name: Property Tax Exemption for Disabled Veterans and Survivors
programs.agency: Vermont Office of Veterans Affairs / local town assessors
programs.eligibility: Veteran (or surviving spouse/dependent) rated 50% or more service-connected disabled by the VA, OR receiving VA Non-Service-Connected Improved Pension, OR receiving military retirement pay for a permanent medical military retirement. Must be the veteran's owned primary residence. Annual proof due before May 1 (one-time for the permanently and totally disabled).
programs.coverage: A minimum of $10,000 of appraised value is exempt by state law; towns may vote to raise the exemption up to $40,000.
programs.notes: Reduces appraised value before taxes are assessed. Applies only to the veteran-owned primary residence.

programs.name: Veteran and Disabled Veteran License Plates
programs.agency: Vermont Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV)
programs.eligibility: Veteran plate: any veteran with a completed Vermont Certificate of Veteran Status (Form VG-168). Disabled Veteran plate: a veteran with a service-connected disability, requiring the VG-168 plus a DMV medical evaluation.
programs.coverage: Special plate issuance. The fee/tax exemption (no sales/use tax, registration fee, or license fee) applies only to disabled veterans whose vehicle was modified for the disability with VA funding (32 V.S.A. § 8911).
programs.notes: The plate itself is the benefit; the registration/sales-tax exemption is narrow (VA-funded vehicle modification only). Requires Form VG-168 certified by the Office of Veterans Affairs.

programs.name: Free Permanent Hunting/Fishing License for Disabled Veterans
programs.agency: Vermont Fish & Wildlife Department
programs.eligibility: Vermont resident veteran who is, or ever has been, 60% or more disabled as a result of a service-connected disability. Requires a VA letter stating the rating; processed at the Fish & Wildlife main office in Montpelier.
programs.coverage: A free permanent fishing, hunting, or combination license, including all big game licenses except moose.
programs.notes: The 60% threshold differs from the 50% threshold for the property tax exemption.

programs.name: Vermont Veterans' Home (Bennington)
programs.agency: Vermont Veterans' Home
programs.eligibility: Veterans who served at least 90 days in the U.S. Armed Forces and were discharged under honorable conditions. Spouses, widows/widowers of honorably discharged veterans, and Gold Star parents/spouses are also eligible. Vermont residency is not required, but Vermont residents receive priority.
programs.coverage: Long-term skilled nursing and residential care; accepts private pay, Medicare, and Vermont Medicaid.
programs.notes: Located in Bennington.

programs.name: Military Retirement & Survivor Benefit Income Tax Exemption
programs.agency: Vermont Department of Taxes
programs.eligibility: Taxpayers of any filing status receiving military retirement pay or survivor benefit income, based on adjusted gross income (AGI).
programs.coverage: FULL exemption of all military retirement and survivor benefit income for AGI ≤ $125,000. Partial exemption phasing out for AGI between $125,000 and $175,000; no exemption at AGI ≥ $175,000.
programs.notes: Act 71 (2025), effective tax year 2025, removed the old $10,000 cap and replaced it with this AGI-tiered full-exemption system. It also created a separate $250 refundable Vermont Veteran Tax Credit for veterans with AGI ≤ $25,000.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran Property Tax Exemption (Clauses 22–22H)
programs.agency: MA Department of Revenue, Division of Local Services (administered by local boards of assessors)
programs.eligibility: Massachusetts-domiciled veteran (or eligible surviving spouse) meeting clause criteria; base Clause 22 requires a 10%+ service-connected VA rating, a Purple Heart, or Gold Star parent status. Higher clauses require greater service-connected loss.
programs.coverage: Tiered exemption amounts (minimums set by state law): Clause 22 $400; 22A $750; 22B $1,250; 22C $1,500; 22E $1,000 (100% service-connected); Clauses 22D/22F/22H = FULL (100%) exemption (e.g., paraplegic veterans or 100% service-connected blindness). Municipalities may grant additional relief by local option.
programs.notes: Exemptions reduce the tax bill, not the assessed value. Apply to the local board of assessors.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran Motor Vehicle Excise Tax Exemption & DV Plate
programs.agency: MA Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV); excise exemption via local board of assessors
programs.eligibility: Excise exemption: veteran with VA-determined service-connected loss/loss of use of limb(s), permanent vision impairment, or 100% disability/unemployability, for one personal vehicle. DV plate: MA resident veteran who is primary owner of a registered passenger vehicle, qualifies for permanent disabled parking, and has a minimum 60% service-connected rating affecting ambulation.
programs.coverage: Full exemption from motor vehicle excise tax on one personal-use vehicle. The excise exemption does not require holding the DV plate, only eligibility.
programs.notes: The excise exemption is applied for at the city/town where the vehicle is registered. The DV plate requires a 60%+ rating; the excise exemption eligibility is broader.

programs.name: Free Hunting/Fishing License for Paraplegic & Disabled Residents
programs.agency: MA Division of Fisheries & Wildlife (MassWildlife)
programs.eligibility: Massachusetts residents who are paraplegic (physician-certified), blind, or have an intellectual disability. Paraplegic eligibility applies to disabled veterans who meet the medical definition.
programs.coverage: FREE freshwater fishing, hunting, or sporting license.
programs.notes: MassWildlife has no distinct blanket 'veteran' free license — the benefit is disability-based (paraplegia), which many disabled veterans qualify for. First-time applicants submit a physician certification form.

programs.name: Massachusetts Veterans Homes (Chelsea & Holyoke)
programs.agency: MA Veterans Homes / Executive Office of Veterans Services
programs.eligibility: Must meet the MA statutory definition of 'veteran' (generally 90+ days active duty with last discharge other than dishonorable, or any service with a service-connected disability); be a Massachusetts resident at time of application; and be medically suitable for long-term nursing/residential care. DD-214 required.
programs.coverage: Residential and long-term nursing care at two homes (Chelsea and Holyoke).
programs.notes: Apply to the respective home's admissions office.

programs.name: State Income Tax on Military Retired Pay (Exempt)
programs.agency: MA Department of Revenue (DOR)
programs.eligibility: All recipients of U.S. uniformed-services military retired pay and military survivor benefits, regardless of age or income.
programs.coverage: 100% exempt from Massachusetts state income tax.
programs.notes: Massachusetts fully exempts military retirement pay plus SBP/RCSBP survivor annuities as noncontributory U.S. service pension income.

programs.name: 100% Disabled Veteran Property Tax Exemption (and Surviving Spouse)
programs.agency: NJ Department of the Treasury, Division of Taxation (administered by the local municipal assessor)
programs.eligibility: Honorably discharged active-duty veteran, NJ legal resident, who owns and occupies the dwelling as principal residence and is certified by the VA as 100% permanently and totally disabled. Surviving spouse/civil union/domestic partner also qualifies if not remarried and the veteran was an NJ resident at death. File Form D.V.S.S.E.
programs.coverage: 100% exemption from local property tax on the veteran's principal residence.
programs.notes: Full exemption on the primary home; separate from the $250 deduction. Denials appealable to the County Board of Taxation by April 1.

programs.name: $250 Veterans Property Tax Deduction
programs.agency: NJ Department of the Treasury, Division of Taxation (administered by the local municipal assessor)
programs.eligibility: Honorably discharged active-duty veteran, NJ legal resident, who owns the property. Reservists/National Guard must have been called to active duty. Surviving spouse/civil union/domestic partner may also qualify if not remarried. File Form V.S.S./V.N.D.A.
programs.coverage: $250 annual deduction from property taxes.
programs.notes: A November 2020 constitutional amendment removed the prior wartime-service requirement (effective tax years 2021+), so eligibility now extends to all honorably discharged active-duty veterans including peacetime service.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran Free Vehicle Registration & DV/Purple Heart Plates
programs.agency: NJ Motor Vehicle Commission (MVC)
programs.eligibility: Free registration for veterans who are blind from war service and eligible for state compensation, OR who have a service-connected disability and qualify for a free automobile from the VA. Disabled Veteran and Purple Heart placards/plates available via Form SP-47.
programs.coverage: Free vehicle registration (100% fee waiver) for qualifying disabled veterans; the DV/Purple Heart placard grants exemption from municipal parking meter fees for up to 24 hours.
programs.notes: Free-registration eligibility is narrow (war-blind or VA automobile-grant disability), not all disabled veterans.

programs.name: Free Hunting & Fishing Licenses for Disabled Veterans
programs.agency: NJ Department of Environmental Protection (NJDEP), Division of Fish & Wildlife
programs.eligibility: Honorably discharged resident veterans declared by the VA to have a service-connected disability of any degree, who are NJ residents. Must be certified by Fish & Wildlife first (by mail to Trenton).
programs.coverage: Free (100%) resident hunting and fishing licenses, permits, and stamps, including unlimited antlerless deer permits and free turkey and bear permits.
programs.notes: Once certified, licenses are free at agents with no transaction fee. A separate program covers NJ National Guard members.

programs.name: New Jersey Veterans Memorial Homes (Menlo Park, Paramus, Vineland)
programs.agency: NJ Department of Military and Veterans Affairs (DMVA)
programs.eligibility: Veterans honorably discharged from war or peacetime service; the veteran's spouse; and spouses/parents of service members killed in action (Gold Star). Spouse/widow(er) must be at least 50 and married to the veteran for at least 10 years. Preference to 2-year NJ residents.
programs.coverage: Long-term skilled nursing / residential care at three state homes; residents pay according to ability to pay based on income.
programs.notes: Three homes: Menlo Park (Edison), Paramus, and Vineland.

programs.name: State Income Tax on Military Retired Pay (Exempt)
programs.agency: NJ Department of the Treasury, Division of Taxation
programs.eligibility: All recipients of U.S. military pension and survivor's benefit payments, regardless of age or disability status.
programs.coverage: 100% exempt from NJ Gross Income Tax (military pension and survivor benefit payments are not taxable and not reported on the NJ return).
programs.notes: Federal civil-service pensions remain taxable in NJ even if based on military-service credit. Honorably discharged veterans also get a separate $6,000 NJ income tax personal exemption.

programs.name: Disabled Veterans Homestead Property Tax Exemption
programs.agency: Michigan Department of Treasury / local assessor (State Tax Commission)
programs.eligibility: Michigan resident veteran honorably discharged who is VA-determined permanently and totally disabled at the 100% rate, holds a VA certificate for specially adapted housing, or is rated individually unemployable (TDIU). Unremarried surviving spouse may continue the exemption. Property must be the homestead.
programs.coverage: 100% exemption from property tax on the homestead (full elimination of the tax bill, not a partial reduction).
programs.notes: Statutory authority MCL 211.7b. A proposed conversion to a refundable credit did not become law; current 2026 law remains a full exemption, and (beginning 2026) an approved exemption auto-renews annually.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran (DV) and Veteran License Plates
programs.agency: Michigan Department of State (Secretary of State)
programs.eligibility: Totally disabled veterans (VA service-connected total/permanent rating, or receiving Armed Forces disability retirement pay) with honorable discharge receive a permanent DV plate for one private passenger vehicle. Per a 2024 law, partially disabled veterans rated 50%–90% also qualify for a DV plate. Surviving spouses may continue/transfer the plate.
programs.coverage: No service fee for the totally-disabled DV plate or its renewal (also exempt from registration tax); the permanent plate does not expire. The 50%–90% partial-disability plate follows standard renewal.
programs.notes: Statutory authority MCL 257.803f. Apply with the Michigan Application for Veteran License Plates plus VA proof.

programs.name: Free Hunting and Fishing Licenses for Disabled Veterans
programs.agency: Michigan Department of Natural Resources (DNR)
programs.eligibility: Michigan resident veteran who is VA-determined permanently and totally disabled at the 100% rate (for disabilities other than blindness), OR rated individually unemployable. VA documentation must be carried.
programs.coverage: Free — any hunting or fishing license that does not require a separate (lottery) application is issued at no charge. 100% disabled veterans, Medal of Honor recipients, and ex-POWs also receive free Recreation Passport entry.
programs.notes: Available at all DNR license retailers or online.

programs.name: Michigan Veteran Homes (Grand Rapids, Chesterfield Township, Marquette)
programs.agency: Michigan Department of Military and Veterans Affairs (DMVA) / Michigan Veteran Homes
programs.eligibility: Honorably discharged member of the U.S. Armed Forces with at least 90 days of active duty; must be a Michigan resident at admission (or an accredited Michigan veteran) and eligible for VA health care or financial assistance for long-term nursing care. Eligible dependents — spouse, surviving spouse, and Gold Star parents — may also be admitted.
programs.coverage: Cost is based on ability to pay. Three skilled-nursing communities: Grand Rapids, Chesterfield Township, and D.J. Jacobetti (Marquette).
programs.notes: Services include long-term skilled nursing, rehabilitation, dementia, and palliative care.

programs.name: State Income Tax on Military Retired Pay (Exempt)
programs.agency: Michigan Department of Treasury
programs.eligibility: Retirees of the U.S. Armed Forces receiving military retired pay; a surviving spouse may claim in case of the retiree's death.
programs.coverage: 100% exempt — military retired pay is fully exempt from Michigan individual income tax with no dollar limit, separate from the general retirement subtraction limits.
programs.notes: Claimed as a subtraction on Michigan Schedule 1 to the extent included in federal AGI.

programs.name: Standard Homestead Exemption for Veterans with Disabilities (SHEVD)
programs.agency: Illinois Department of Revenue / County Assessor (35 ILCS 200/15-169)
programs.eligibility: Illinois resident veteran with a VA-certified service-connected disability of at least 30%, who owns and occupies the property as primary residence. Surviving spouses may continue the exemption.
programs.coverage: Tiered EAV reduction: 30–49% disability = $2,500 EAV; 50–69% = $5,000 EAV; 70% or more = the first $250,000 of EAV fully exempt (can result in zero property tax on the home).
programs.notes: Veterans rated 100% permanent & total are auto-renewed annually. Applies only to the residential primary residence.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran (DV) License Plates
programs.agency: Illinois Secretary of State (Vehicle Services)
programs.eligibility: U.S. Armed Forces veteran with proof of a service-connected disability from the VA AND certification from a licensed physician that the disability qualifies for a disabled plate/placard.
programs.coverage: First set of plates issued at no cost with a $0 annual registration renewal fee. A second set carries standard fees. Plates allow parking in disabled-reserved spaces.
programs.notes: A related Service-Connected Disabled Veteran (ISERVE) plate also exists.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran Hunting & Fishing License
programs.agency: Illinois Department of Natural Resources / Illinois Department of Veterans Affairs (IDVA)
programs.eligibility: Veteran receiving 10% or greater service-connected compensation, or a total disability pension. Requires a DD-214 and a Disability Affidavit obtained through an IDVA Veteran Service Office. Available regardless of state of residency.
programs.coverage: Free of charge, issued as a one-time, no-expiration license. Also exempt from the habitat stamp; disabled veterans and former POWs may camp free in IDNR state parks.
programs.notes: Made permanent (one-time issue) per IDVA.

programs.name: Illinois Veterans' Homes (Anna, Chicago, LaSalle, Manteno, Quincy)
programs.agency: Illinois Department of Veterans Affairs (IDVA)
programs.eligibility: Honorably discharged veteran with at least one day of active duty who has service credited to Illinois OR resided in Illinois for at least one year before applying. Eligible spouses, widows/widowers, and Gold Star family members may also qualify.
programs.coverage: Skilled nursing and domiciliary care across five homes. Admission is not based on ability to pay; the maximum monthly resident contribution is $1,659, calculated from the veteran's monthly income.
programs.notes: Priority for admission to veterans who served during a time of conflict.

programs.name: State Income Tax on Military Retired Pay (Exempt)
programs.agency: Illinois Department of Revenue
programs.eligibility: Any recipient of federally taxed military retirement/pension income (all branches, National Guard, and Reserves). No age requirement and no income cap.
programs.coverage: 100% exempt. The federally taxed portion of government/military retirement income is subtracted on Form IL-1040 (Illinois does not tax retirement income).
programs.notes: Confirmed via IL DOR Publication 120. Blended Retirement System TSP distributions also qualify; must be manually entered on the subtraction line.

programs.name: Wyoming Veterans Property Tax Exemption
programs.agency: Wyoming Department of Revenue, Property Tax Division (administered by County Assessor/Treasurer)
programs.eligibility: Honorably discharged wartime veterans (or recipients of specified service medals for foreign service). Must be a current Wyoming resident for at least 3 years. Certain permanently/totally service-connected disabled veterans and surviving spouses (until remarriage) may also qualify.
programs.coverage: $6,000 of assessed value (increased from $3,000 effective the 2025 tax year per SF0089 / W.S. 39-13-105(b)); roughly a $400 property tax reduction. Alternatively applies to the county motor vehicle registration fee.
programs.notes: Property tax applications due by the 4th Monday in May; the vehicle-registration use can be claimed anytime during the year. The exemption applies to property tax OR vehicle registration, not both.

programs.name: Veteran / Disabled Veteran License Plates & Registration Fee Exemption
programs.agency: Wyoming Military Department (Veterans Commission) / County Treasurer
programs.eligibility: Veterans for military-related plates (including disabled veteran plates); the vehicle must be titled in the veteran's name or jointly with an immediate family member. The Veterans Property Tax Exemption may be applied to the county vehicle registration fee in lieu of property tax.
programs.coverage: Approximately a $180 reduction in the vehicle registration fee when the $6,000 assessed-value exemption is applied to registration; special veteran/disabled-veteran plates available.
programs.notes: The property tax exemption and the vehicle registration fee reduction are the same single annual exemption applied to one or the other.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran / Purple Heart Hunting & Fishing Licenses
programs.agency: Wyoming Game & Fish Department
programs.eligibility: Wyoming resident veterans. 100% VA-rated disabled resident veterans (honorable discharge) qualify for free lifetime licenses; 50% disabled resident veterans qualify for a reduced lifetime fishing license; Purple Heart recipients qualify for free lifetime licenses.
programs.coverage: Free lifetime game bird, small game, and fishing licenses for 100% disabled veterans and Purple Heart recipients; a reduced-cost lifetime fishing license for 50%-disabled veterans. Valid as long as the licensee remains a Wyoming resident.
programs.notes: Active-duty residents deployed to combat zones also receive complimentary resident licenses while on leave.

programs.name: Veterans' Home of Wyoming (Buffalo)
programs.agency: Wyoming Department of Health (Aging Division)
programs.eligibility: Honorably discharged veterans, dependents of qualified veterans, or qualified non-veterans (as space allows). Must hold valid Wyoming residence at application (or intent to permanently reside) and be unable to earn a living due to wounds/disease/age/infirmity or lack adequate means of support.
programs.coverage: Residents' fees are based on individual ability to pay; the monthly maintenance fee covers a private room, meals, laundry, nursing, social services, activities, and weekday transportation.
programs.notes: Located in Buffalo. Admission includes a two-day trial stay. Contact (307) 684-5511.

programs.name: State Income Tax on Military Retired Pay (None)
programs.agency: Wyoming Department of Revenue
programs.eligibility: All residents, including military retirees.
programs.coverage: Wyoming has NO state personal income tax. Military retired pay is not taxed at the state level.
programs.notes: One of the states with no individual income tax, so military retirement, pension, and all other income are exempt from state income tax.

programs.name: Disabled Veterans' Homestead Deduction
programs.agency: DC Office of Tax and Revenue (OTR) / Mayor's Office of Community Affairs
programs.eligibility: Veteran classified by the VA as total and permanent service-connected disabled, or paid at the 100% rate due to individual unemployability. Property must be the principal residence in DC; the veteran must hold at least 50% ownership and be domiciled in DC. Total household income must be below the relief limit ($163,500 for TY 2026).
programs.coverage: Reduces the property's assessed value by $445,000.
programs.notes: Effective October 1, 2022. A property receiving this deduction cannot also take the regular Homestead deduction, Senior/Disabled Tax Relief, or the tax-cap credit.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran / Veteran License Plates & Fee Waiver
programs.agency: DC Department of Motor Vehicles (DC DMV)
programs.eligibility: Disabled American Veteran (DAV) tags require certification of DAV membership by the DC DAV Commander. The fee waiver requires a VA letter indicating a service-connected disability rated 'Total and Permanent.'
programs.coverage: One set of tags at no fee for a non-commercial vehicle for service-connected permanent-and-total disabled veterans. Standard (non-disabled) Veteran specialty tags cost a one-time $52 fee plus $26 annually.
programs.notes: DC offers both DAV tags and general Veteran specialty tags. The fee waiver is limited to one set of tags per qualifying P&T disabled veteran.

programs.name: DC Fishing License (No Veteran-Specific Discount)
programs.agency: DC Department of Energy & Environment (DOEE)
programs.eligibility: Anyone age 16 to 64 fishing in DC waters must hold a current DC fishing license. Exempt: persons under 16 and persons 65 or older.
programs.coverage: DC resident license $10/year; non-resident $13/year. No veteran or disability discount or waiver — the only fee exemptions are age-based.
programs.notes: DC is fully urban and issues only fishing (not hunting) licenses. Documented here to show the absence of a veteran-specific benefit in this category.

programs.name: Long-Term Care for Veterans (No DC Veterans Home)
programs.agency: Federal — Armed Forces Retirement Home (AFRH) and VA Medical Center; DC Mayor's Office of Veterans Affairs for referral
programs.eligibility: AFRH (Washington campus): generally veterans 60+ who served at least 20 years on active duty, plus other combat/disability/wartime categories. Not a DC-administered benefit.
programs.coverage: AFRH offers a continuum of care (independent living, assisted living, memory support, rehab, long-term skilled nursing); resident fees are income-based.
programs.notes: The District of Columbia does NOT operate a veterans home. DC veterans needing long-term care typically use the federal Armed Forces Retirement Home or the VA Medical Center. Listed for accuracy; this is a federal, not DC-local, program.

programs.name: DC Income Tax on Military Retired Pay (Fully Taxable)
programs.agency: DC Office of Tax and Revenue (OTR)
programs.eligibility: All DC residents receiving military retired pay.
programs.coverage: No exclusion — military retired pay is fully included in DC gross income and taxed at ordinary DC individual income tax rates.
programs.notes: DC does NOT offer a military retirement exclusion. The former $3,000 exclusion (age 62+) was repealed effective for tax years beginning on or after Jan 1, 2015. As of 2026 DC fully taxes military retirement pay.

programs.name: Veteran Property Tax (CRIM) Exemption — Regular & Disabled-Veteran Enhanced
programs.agency: Centro de Recaudación de Ingresos Municipales (CRIM); established by the Carta de Derechos del Veterano (Ley 203-2007)
programs.eligibility: Puerto Rico resident veterans of the U.S. Armed Forces, on their primary residence. Enhanced exemptions apply to veterans with VA service-connected disability ratings.
programs.coverage: All veterans: $5,000 reduction in appraised taxable value. Veterans rated 50%+ service-connected disabled: exemption on the first $50,000 of appraised value. Veterans rated 100% disabled: complete property tax exemption on the primary residence.
programs.notes: Granted in addition to the standard residential exoneration. Apply through CRIM with VA disability certification.

programs.name: Veteran Vehicle Excise Benefit & Veteran License Plate
programs.agency: Departamento de Hacienda (excise) and DTOP/CESCO (registration and plates)
programs.eligibility: Puerto Rico resident veterans. Full exemption tiers for veterans rated 100% disabled and for veterans age 60 or older.
programs.coverage: One free veteran license plate (tablilla de veterano); additional plates $10 each. Veterans rated 100% disabled and veterans age 60+ are fully exempt from vehicle excise tax, plate fees, and driver's license fees. The general veteran vehicle excise incentive applies up to a $5,000 vehicle value.
programs.notes: Plate/exemption tiers established under the Carta de Derechos del Veterano.

programs.name: Casa del Veterano (Long-Term Care Facility)
programs.agency: Oficina del Procurador del Veterano (OPV) — Gobierno de Puerto Rico
programs.eligibility: Veterans (men and women) of the U.S. Armed Forces; admission via OPV admissions orientation.
programs.coverage: A 240-bed territorial facility (120 skilled nursing + 120 domiciliary beds) providing affordable long-term care, including medical, nursing, social work, rehabilitation, meals, laundry, and recreation.
programs.notes: Puerto Rico's territorial veterans home, distinct from the federal VA Caribbean Healthcare System hospital. Located in Juana Díaz.

programs.name: Income Tax on Military Retired Pay (Exempt — Ley 191-2024)
programs.agency: Departamento de Hacienda de Puerto Rico
programs.eligibility: Puerto Rico-resident veterans who are retired members of the U.S. Armed Forces.
programs.coverage: 100% exemption from Puerto Rico income tax on military retirement pension income, starting with the 2025 tax year. Veterans also receive a $1,500 additional personal exemption ($3,000 if both spouses are veterans).
programs.notes: Enacted by Ley Núm. 191 de 2024 (signed Aug 29, 2024), amending the Código de Rentas Internas. Separate from the pre-existing $1,500 veteran personal exemption.

programs.name: 100% Disabled Veteran / Surviving Spouse / Gold Star Real Property Tax Exemption
programs.agency: Guam Department of Revenue and Taxation, Real Property Tax Division
programs.eligibility: Veteran rated by the VA as 100% disabled or individually unemployable due to service-connected injuries; an unremarried surviving spouse; a legal guardian; or a Gold Star spouse/parent. Must own and occupy the property as a residence.
programs.coverage: Full exemption from Guam real property taxes (100%) on one residence; commercial portions are not exempt.
programs.notes: Authorized by Public Law 34-106 (Title 11, Chapter 24 GCA). File with the assessor's office by March 15 with a VA Benefit Information letter.

programs.name: Veteran and Disabled Veteran License Plates
programs.agency: Guam Department of Revenue and Taxation, Motor Vehicle Division
programs.eligibility: Resident veterans with an other-than-dishonorable discharge. Disability decals/symbols available with proof of disability and military service.
programs.coverage: Specialty veteran/disabled-veteran plates issued by the MVD; 100%-disabled veterans are separately eligible for a Guam license and registration fee waiver. Exact plate fees are not published online (contact the Vehicle Registration Branch).
programs.notes: The MVD issues veteran's plates and disabled parking placards/plates.

programs.name: Guam Veterans Cemetery (Territorial Burial Benefit)
programs.agency: Guam Veterans Affairs Office (GVAO), under the Office of the Governor
programs.eligibility: All eligible veterans and their eligible dependents (spouse, minor children, and certain disabled adult children).
programs.coverage: A territorial veterans cemetery operated and maintained by the Guam government; interment for eligible veterans and dependents.
programs.notes: Guam's genuine territorial long-term/end-of-life veterans benefit (built/expanded with VA National Cemetery Administration grant funds). There is NO territorial veterans nursing home on Guam; long-term care runs through the federal VA Pacific Islands clinic or private facilities.

programs.name: Guam Territorial Income Tax on Military Retired Pay (Taxable)
programs.agency: Guam Department of Revenue and Taxation
programs.eligibility: Bona fide Guam residents who file the Guam Territorial Income Tax with Guam DRT.
programs.coverage: No exclusion — military retired pay is fully taxable. Guam has not adopted a separate military retirement exclusion.
programs.notes: Guam uses a 'mirror code' — the U.S. Internal Revenue Code applied as the Guam Territorial Income Tax (filed with Guam DRT, not the IRS). Active-duty pay of nonresidents stationed on Guam is protected under the SCRA, distinct from retired pay.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran Property Tax Exemption (Homestead)
programs.agency: USVI Office of the Lt. Governor — Office of the Tax Assessor (coordinated by USVI Office of Veterans Affairs)
programs.eligibility: Veteran with a discharge other than dishonorable who holds a VA service-connected total and permanent (100% P&T) disability rating; must own and occupy the property as of January 1 and apply before March 1. Surviving spouses may also qualify.
programs.coverage: 100% exemption from all property taxes for 100% P&T disabled veterans. Non-disabled eligible veterans/surviving spouses receive a $650 property tax credit instead.
programs.notes: Apply through the island Tax Assessor's Office (St. Croix 340-773-6449; St. Thomas/St. John 340-774-2991).

programs.name: Veteran & Disabled Veteran Specialty License Plates
programs.agency: USVI Bureau of Motor Vehicles, in coordination with the USVI Office of Veterans Affairs
programs.eligibility: Honorably (other-than-dishonorably) discharged veterans; disabled-veteran plate for VA-rated disabled veterans; Gold Star plate for eligible surviving family members.
programs.coverage: Specialty plate issued free of charge; standard vehicle registration fees still apply.
programs.notes: Three plate types: USVI Veteran, USVI Disabled Veteran, and USVI Gold Star Family. A free 'Veteran' designation can also be added to a USVI driver's license.

programs.name: Income Tax on Military Retired Pay (Mirror Code, Taxable)
programs.agency: Virgin Islands Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR)
programs.eligibility: All bona fide USVI residents, including retired servicemembers, who file with the BIR rather than the IRS.
programs.coverage: No exemption — military retired pay is fully taxable under the USVI 'mirror' of the U.S. Internal Revenue Code, at the same rates and rules as federal income tax.
programs.notes: USVI residents pay income tax to the BIR, not the IRS. Military DISABILITY retirement pay is excluded from gross income under the federal/mirror code (a federal exclusion, not a USVI-specific veteran benefit). NOTE: the USVI does not operate a territorial veterans home, and there is no veteran-specific hunting/fishing discount; USVI veterans rely on the federal VA Caribbean Healthcare System.

programs.name: Income Tax Treatment of Military Retired Pay (Taxable)
programs.agency: American Samoa Government Tax Office (ASG Department of Treasury)
programs.eligibility: Bona fide residents of American Samoa who receive U.S. military retired pay and file an American Samoa individual income tax return.
programs.coverage: American Samoa operates its own income tax code (modeled on the U.S. IRC but not a pure mirror). Military retired pay is taxable; there is no general veteran retired-pay exemption. Military disability retirement pay for a service-connected injury/sickness is excluded from income, consistent with IRC treatment.
programs.notes: Residents file with the ASG Tax Office, not the IRS. Verify current-year details directly with the ASG Tax Office.

programs.name: Reliance on Federal VA Care (No Territorial Veterans Home or Property Tax)
programs.agency: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (federal); coordinated locally with the ASG Office of Veterans & Military Affairs
programs.eligibility: Veterans residing in American Samoa enrolled in VA health care.
programs.coverage: American Samoa has NO territorial veterans home or long-term care facility, and NO conventional real property tax (land is largely communally owned). Veterans rely on the federal VA Clinic and Vet Center in Pago Pago; complex/inpatient/long-term care generally requires off-island VA referral.
programs.notes: American Samoa offers essentially no territory-specific veteran benefits beyond income-tax treatment; benefits are federal VA programs. The ASG Office of Veterans & Military Affairs functions primarily as a claims/connection liaison. No veteran-specific vehicle-plate or hunting/fishing program could be confirmed.

programs.name: Veteran, Disabled Veteran, and Gold Star License Plates
programs.agency: CNMI Department of Public Safety, Bureau of Motor Vehicles
programs.eligibility: Veterans discharged under conditions other than dishonorable (Veteran plate); 10%+ VA disability rating (Disabled Veteran plate); surviving family of a service member who died on active duty (Gold Star plate). Non-commercial passenger vehicles and motorcycles.
programs.coverage: Issuance and renewal fees are 25% less than the comparable plate fee. Veterans rated 100% permanent and total by the VA pay no issuance fee.
programs.notes: Authorized by 9 CMC Section 2116. Contact the CNMI Office of Veterans Affairs at 670-664-2650.

programs.name: CNMI Veterans Cemetery
programs.agency: CNMI Office of Veterans Affairs (Office of the Governor)
programs.eligibility: Eligible service members, veterans, and their qualifying family members; burial eligibility conforms to U.S. VA National Cemetery Administration standards.
programs.coverage: Burial and interment at the CNMI Veterans Cemetery (Marpi, Saipan). Commonwealth-owned, opened Nov 11, 2006, built with a U.S. VA grant.
programs.notes: The only territorial veterans facility. The CNMI has NO veterans home or long-term care facility; veterans rely on the federal VA (Saipan VA outreach clinic, intermittent) and off-island VA care.

programs.name: Income Tax on Military Retired Pay (NMTIT, Taxable)
programs.agency: CNMI Department of Finance, Division of Revenue and Taxation
programs.eligibility: Bona fide CNMI residents who receive military retired pay.
programs.coverage: No territorial exemption — military retired pay is taxable. The CNMI levies the Northern Marianas Territorial Income Tax (NMTIT), a mirror of the U.S. IRC, filed locally. Military disability retirement pay for a service-connected injury/sickness is excluded, mirroring the federal exclusion.
programs.notes: No veteran-specific subtraction for retired pay exists; treatment follows the federal mirror code. The CNMI has no annual real property tax, so no veteran property-tax exemption exists.
